# Remesh
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/3d-model/remesh

# Remesh

Regenerate a model's mesh topology, optimizing face count and arrangement so AI-generated meshes become production-ready.

---

## TL;DR
- Regenerates a model's mesh topology, optimizing face count and face arrangement.

- You can specify a target polygon count to balance quality and performance.

- AI-generated models typically have excessive triangles and irregular topology — Remesh makes them production-ready.

- Required before 3D printing to ensure a watertight (hole-free, closed) mesh.

---

## When to Use
- The model's face count is too high and needs to be reduced (games: under 50K, mobile: under 10K).

- The model needs to be 3D printed — watertight mesh is mandatory.

- You need cleaner topology for downstream operations (UV unwrapping, animation rigging, etc.).

---

## When NOT to Use
- The model already has acceptable face count and good topology.

- You're in the concept exploration phase — Remesh only the final asset.

---

## Step-by-Step
1. Select the target model.

2. Enter the **Remesh** tool.

3. Set the **Target Polygon Count** (e.g., 10K faces).

4. Click **Remesh** and wait for processing.

5. Compare the original and remeshed model: check detail preservation.

6. If satisfied, replace or save as a new model.

![Meshy Remesh settings: choose a fixed or adaptive target polycount and quad or triangle topology before regenerating the mesh](https://cdn.meshy.ai/webapp-assets/doc/remesh-p0-1.webp)

---

## Settings & Tradeoffs
| Target Faces | Use Case | Detail Loss | File Size |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| < 5K | Mobile AR, casual games | Noticeable | Small |
| 5K – 20K | Mobile games, web viewers | Minor | Medium |
| 20K – 50K | PC/console games | Minimal | Medium |
| 50K – 100K | High-quality renders | Very low | Large |
| > 100K | Film/cinematic | Negligible | Very large |

---

## Troubleshooting
| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Severe detail loss | Target face count too low | Increase target count; find the quality-performance balance |
| Holes after remeshing | Original mesh has non-manifold edges | Try a higher face count, or repair the original mesh first |
| Small accessories disappear | Uneven face budget distribution | Remesh complex models part by part |

---

## FAQ
### What does Remesh do in Meshy?

Remesh regenerates a model's topology, optimizing face count and arrangement so AI-generated meshes become production-ready.

### How many polygons should a game model have?

Aim for under ~50K faces for PC games and under ~10K for mobile; set your target polygon count in the Remesh tool.

### Do I need to Remesh before 3D printing?

Yes. Remesh can produce a watertight (hole-free, closed) mesh, which is mandatory for successful 3D printing.

### Will Remesh reduce my model's detail?

Lower targets trade some detail for performance; compare the original and remeshed versions and raise the target if needed.

### When should I Remesh in my workflow?

Remesh the final asset before UV unwrapping, texturing, or rigging — skip it during concept exploration.

---

## Related Links
- [AI Texturing](/webapp/guides/3d-model/ai-texturing) — Retexturing after Remesh produces better results

- [Unwrap UV](/webapp/guides/3d-model/unwrap-uv) — UV needs to be regenerated after Remesh

- [Rigging](/webapp/guides/3d-model/rigging) — Clean topology is essential for rigging

---

# Rigging
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/3d-model/rigging

# Rigging

Automatically bind skeletons to humanoid and quadruped models, preparing characters for animation and export to Unity, Unreal, and other engines.

---

## TL;DR
- Automatically binds skeletons to humanoid and quadruped models.

- Rigged models can be used directly for animation or exported to Unity/Unreal with Mixamo-compatible animation libraries.

- Depends on clean topology: Remesh first, then Rig for best results.

---

## When to Use
- You want generated characters to move (walk, run, attack, etc.).

- You need to import models into game engines with ready-to-use animations.

---

## When NOT to Use
- The model is not a character type (e.g., props, buildings, vehicles).

- You need complex custom skeletons (facial expressions, tail physics) → Export and manually rig in DCC tools.

---

## Step-by-Step
1. Select a humanoid or quadruped character model.

2. Enter the **Rigging** tool.

3. The system automatically detects model type and assigns a skeleton structure.

4. Preview bone binding and weight assignment.

5. Test basic poses (T-pose, A-pose switching).

6. Confirm and export as FBX (with rig) or proceed to Animate within Meshy.

![Meshy Rig Model panel: place body markers like chin, shoulders, and knees on the character, with symmetry enabled for precise auto-rigging](https://cdn.meshy.ai/webapp-assets/doc/rigging-p0-1.webp)

---

## Troubleshooting
| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bone positions are offset | Model pose is non-standard | Ensure the input model is close to T-pose or A-pose |
| Weight penetration (clipping) | Topology too dense or uneven | Remesh to a reasonable face count before rigging |
| Severe limb deformation | Abnormal model proportions | Ensure character proportions are close to standard human body |

---

## FAQ
### How do I rig a 3D character in Meshy?

Select a humanoid or quadruped model, open the Rigging tool, and Meshy auto-detects the type and assigns a skeleton.

### What models can Meshy auto-rig?

Humanoid and quadruped characters. Props, buildings, and vehicles cannot be rigged.

### Is Meshy rigging compatible with Unity and Unreal?

Yes. Rigged models export as FBX and work with Mixamo-compatible animation libraries in Unity and Unreal.

### Should I Remesh before rigging?

Yes. Clean topology gives the most accurate bone binding and weight assignment, so Remesh first.

### Can I rig a model for facial expressions or tail physics?

Not directly — for complex custom skeletons, export the model and rig manually in a DCC tool like Blender or Maya.

---

## Related Links
- [Animate](/webapp/guides/animate) — Proceed to animation after rigging

- [Remesh](/webapp/guides/3d-model/remesh) — Optimize topology before rigging

---

# Unwrap UV
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/3d-model/unwrap-uv

# Unwrap UV

Automatically generate clean UV layouts, preparing models for manual texturing or AI Texturing — good UV means no seams, no stretching.

---

## TL;DR
- Automatically generates UV unwrap layouts, preparing models for manual texturing or AI Texturing.

- UV quality directly impacts texture results — good UV = no seams, no stretching.

- Recommended to run after Remesh and before AI Texturing.

---

## When to Use
- UV was lost after Remesh and needs to be regenerated.

- An imported external model has no UV.

- AI Texturing results show visible seams — better UV layout is needed.

---

## When NOT to Use
- Your model already has high-quality UV (carefully crafted in a DCC tool).

- You don't need textures (e.g., STL export for 3D printing only needs geometry).

---

## Step-by-Step
1. Select the target model.

2. Enter the **Unwrap UV** tool.

3. The system automatically calculates the optimal UV layout.

4. Preview the UV island arrangement and check for excessive stretching.

5. Confirm and save — you can now proceed to AI Texturing.

---

## FAQ
### What does Unwrap UV do?

It automatically generates a clean UV layout, unwrapping your 3D surface into 2D space so textures apply without seams or stretching.

### When should I use Unwrap UV?

Use it after Remesh, when an imported model has no UVs, or when AI Texturing shows visible seams.

### Do I need to Unwrap UV before AI Texturing?

It's recommended — good UVs are the foundation for high-quality, seam-free textures.

### Does Remesh remove my model's UVs?

Yes. Remesh rebuilds topology, so you should regenerate UVs with Unwrap UV afterward.

### When can I skip UV unwrapping?

Skip it if your model already has high-quality UVs, or if you only need geometry (e.g., STL for 3D printing).

---

## Related Links
- [AI Texturing](/webapp/guides/3d-model/ai-texturing) — Good UV is the foundation for high-quality textures

- [Remesh](/webapp/guides/3d-model/remesh) — Remesh rebuilds topology, requiring UV regeneration

---

# Animation
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/animate

# Animation

Auto-rig humanoid and quadruped characters and apply 500+ animation presets, then export rigged FBX or GLB for Unity, Unreal, and Blender pipelines.

---

## TL;DR
- Auto-rigs humanoid/quadruped characters and applies animation presets.

- 500+ built-in animation presets across categories: walk & run, body movements, daily actions, fighting moves, and more.

- Exports rigged and animated models as FBX or GLB, compatible with Unity/Unreal/Blender.

---

## When to Use
- You have a 3D character and need rigging + animation in one step.

- You want to quickly apply standard motion clips (idle, walk, run, attack, etc.) without manual keyframing.

- You need to preview how a character reads in motion before committing to a full animation pipeline.

---

## When NOT to Use
- You need custom choreographed motion not covered by presets → Export the rigged FBX, then animate manually in Blender/Maya or retarget Mixamo animations.

- You need cinematic-level precise animation with facial expressions → Manually create in Maya/Blender.

- The character has a non-standard body plan that auto-rig cannot recognize.

---

## Step-by-Step
1. Select a model (T-pose or A-pose recommended for best rigging results).

2. Enter the Animate module.

3. Auto-rig is applied automatically (humanoid or quadruped skeleton).

4. Browse the animation preset library (500+ presets) and select the desired motion.

5. Preview the animation in 3D viewer.

6. Add multiple animation clips if needed.

7. Export as FBX (with skeleton + animation data) or GLB.

![Meshy Animate module: browse the animation preset library and apply clips like dances and gestures to a rigged character](https://cdn.meshy.ai/webapp-assets/doc/animation-p0-1.webp)

---

## Tips
- Generate characters in T-pose or A-pose for the most accurate auto-rig results.

- For custom animations beyond the preset library, export the rigged FBX and retarget Mixamo clips or author custom keyframes in Blender's Action Editor.

---

## FAQ
### How do I animate a 3D character in Meshy?

Open the Animate module, let auto-rig run, browse the 500+ preset library, pick a motion, preview it, and export.

### How many animation presets does Meshy have?

Over 500 presets across walk & run, body movements, daily actions, fighting moves, and more.

### Can I animate a model I made outside Meshy?

Yes. You can upload an existing model for rigging and animation — T-pose or A-pose works best.

### What formats can I export animated models in?

FBX (with skeleton and animation data) or GLB, compatible with Unity, Unreal, and Blender.

### Can I create custom animations not in the library?

For custom motion, export the rigged FBX and author keyframes or retarget Mixamo clips in Blender or Maya.

---

## Related Links
- [Rigging](/webapp/guides/3d-model/rigging) — Required step before animation

- [3D Agent](/webapp/3d-agent) — Style-consistent batch concept generation through chat

# Choosing: Generation Method
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/choosing/generation-method

# Choosing: Generation Method

Compare Text to 3D, Image to 3D, Multi-view, and 3D Agent to pick the best 3D generation method for your inputs, precision, and process.

---

## TL;DR
- **Text to 3D**: Best for concept exploration, no reference image needed, batch variants.

- **Image to 3D**: Best with a clear visual reference, precise matching, product photos.

- **Multi-view Images to 3D**: Best for high-fidelity multi-angle reconstruction with multiple reference photos.

- **3D Agent**: Best for guided creative process, brainstorming, style-consistent batch concepts, and makers without modeling experience.

- There is no single "best method" — it depends on your input materials, precision needs, and creative process.

---

## Decision Matrix
| Factor | Text to 3D | Image to 3D | Multi-view | 3D Agent |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reference image needed? | ❌ None | ✅ 1 image | ✅ 2–8 images | ⚠️ Optional |
| Precision | ★★★☆☆ | ★★★★☆ | ★★★★★ | ★★★☆☆ |
| Speed | ★★★★☆ | ★★★★☆ | ★★★☆☆ | ★★★☆☆ |
| Creative freedom | ★★★★★ | ★★★☆☆ | ★★☆☆☆ | ★★★★★ |
| Consistency (multi-gen) | ★★☆☆☆ | ★★★★☆ | ★★★★★ | ★★★★☆ |
| Back-side accuracy | ★★★☆☆ | ★★★☆☆ | ★★★★★ | ★★★☆☆ |
| Batch production | ✅ | ✅ (Batch) | ⚠️ Needs prep | ✅ In conversation |
| Guided creative process | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| Built-in Q&A | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |

---

## When to Choose What
**Choose Text to 3D when:**

- You're in the exploration phase and want to quickly try different directions.

- You have no reference image — just a concept in your head.

- You want precise control over style and material via prompts.

**Choose Image to 3D when:**

- You have a concept image, product photo, or sketch.

- You need the result to precisely match a reference image.

- You're doing e-commerce product 3D conversion.

**Choose Multi-view when:**

- You have multiple angles of a physical object.

- You need 360° high-fidelity reconstruction.

- You're doing product digitization scanning.

**Choose 3D Agent when:**

- You want help figuring out what to create in the first place.

- You need batch concepts with consistent style (e.g., a set of game props).

- You're a maker who knows how to print but doesn't know how to model.

- You want to ask 3D creation/printing questions as part of the workflow.

---

## FAQ
### Should I use Text to 3D or Image to 3D?

Use Text to 3D for concept exploration without a reference; use Image to 3D when you have a photo or sketch and need precise matching.

### What is Multi-view Images to 3D best for?

High-fidelity reconstruction when you have multiple angles of the same object, such as product digitization.

### When should I use the 3D Agent instead?

When you want help deciding what to create, need style-consistent batch concepts, or prefer a guided, conversational workflow.

### Which Meshy method is most accurate?

Image to 3D and Multi-view give the most precise results because they work from real visual references.

### Is there one best 3D generation method?

No. The right choice depends on your input materials, precision needs, and how much creative guidance you want.

---

## Related Links
- [Text to 3D](/webapp/text-to-3d)
- [Image to 3D](/webapp/image-to-3d)
- [3D Agent](/webapp/3d-agent)

# Choosing: Integration
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/choosing/integration

# Choosing: Integration

Compare the Meshy Web App, 3D Agent, and REST API to choose the right way to create 3D, whether UI-driven, conversational, or fully automated.

---

## TL;DR
- **Web App**: Simplest, best for individual users and small teams, UI-driven with no coding required.

- **3D Agent**: Conversational, best for brainstorming, guided creation, and makers without modeling experience.

- **API**: Best for automation, batch processing, and product integration.

---

## Comparison
| Factor | Web App | 3D Agent | API |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Learning curve | ★☆☆☆☆ Easiest | ★☆☆☆☆ Just chat | ★★★☆☆ Coding |
| Automation | ❌ | ⚠️ Limited | ✅ Fully automated |
| Batch processing | ⚠️ Batch feature | ✅ In conversation | ✅ Unlimited |
| Tool integration | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ Any system |
| Real-time preview | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ Build your own |
| Brainstorming | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ |
| Best for | Individuals/designers | Makers/creators | Developers/teams |

---

## FAQ
### Should I use the Meshy Web App, 3D Agent, or API?

Use the Web App for UI-driven creation, the 3D Agent for conversational guided creation, and the API for automation and integration.

### Does the Meshy Web App require coding?

No. The Web App is fully UI-driven and needs no coding — best for individuals and small teams.

### When should I use the Meshy API?

For automation, large-scale batch processing, and integrating 3D generation into your own product or pipeline.

### Who is the 3D Agent best for?

Makers and creators who want brainstorming, guided creation, and style-consistent batches without modeling experience.

### Can I switch between the Web App, Agent, and API?

Yes. They share the same Meshy account and models, so you can move between them as your needs change.

# Choosing: Post-Processing
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/choosing/post-processing

# Choosing: Post-Processing

Decide when to Remesh, AI Texture, Unwrap UV, or Rig a 3D model in Meshy using a simple decision flow that keeps assets clean and production-ready.

---

## TL;DR
- **Remesh**: Face count too high, poor topology, need watertight (3D printing).

- **AI Texturing**: Texture quality insufficient, want a style change, need PBR maps.

- **Unwrap UV**: Texture seams visible, need to hand-paint textures.

- **Rigging**: Character needs animation.

---

## Decision Flowchart
```
Model generated
  ├─ Need lower face count? → Remesh
  ├─ Textures unsatisfying? → AI Texturing
  │    └─ Still have seams? → Unwrap UV → AI Texturing
  ├─ Need animation? → Remesh (clean topo) → Rigging → Animate
  └─ Ready to export ✅
```

---

## FAQ
### When should I Remesh a model?

When the face count is too high, topology is messy, or you need a watertight mesh for 3D printing.

### When should I re-texture with AI Texturing?

When texture quality is insufficient, you want a different style, or you need a full PBR map set.

### When do I need to Unwrap UV?

When textures show visible seams or you plan to hand-paint textures in a DCC tool.

### When should I rig a model?

When a character needs to be animated — rig after cleaning topology with Remesh.

### What's the right order for post-processing?

Remesh → Unwrap UV → AI Texturing → Rigging → Animate, then export.

---

## Related Links
- [Remesh](/webapp/guides/3d-model/remesh)
- [AI Texturing](/webapp/guides/3d-model/ai-texturing)
- [Rigging](/webapp/guides/3d-model/rigging)

# AI Image Generation
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/image/ai-image-generation

# AI Image Generation

Generate 2D images from text descriptions, optimized as input for Image to 3D — giving you precise visual style control before entering the 3D pipeline.

---

## TL;DR
- Generate 2D images from text descriptions, optimized as input for Image to 3D.

- Ideal when you have no reference image and want to quickly generate concept art.

- Outputs high-quality PNG, optimized for 3D conversion (clear subject, clean background).

- Difference from Text to 3D: here you generate 2D first, then convert to 3D — giving more precise visual style control.

---

## When to Use
- You have a concept but no reference image and want to visualize it before converting to 3D.

- You want fine-grained control over 2D visual style before entering the 3D pipeline.

---

## When NOT to Use
- You already have a reference image → Go directly to Image to 3D

- You want a one-step text-to-3D result → Use Text to 3D

- You want a guided creative process → Use 3D Agent for brainstorming and concept exploration

---

## Step-by-Step
1. Enter the **Image** module → **AI Image Generation**.

2. Enter a description (e.g., "a low-poly cartoon fox sitting, front view, white background").

3. Select a style preset (e.g., Realistic, Anime, Chibi).

4. Click Generate and wait.

5. Choose the best result from multiple candidates.

6. Click "Send to Image to 3D" to enter the 3D generation pipeline directly.

![Meshy AI Image Generation workspace: text prompts produce 3D-ready concept images like low-poly foxes and wizard characters, with aspect ratio and stylization controls](https://cdn.meshy.ai/webapp-assets/doc/ai-image-generation-p1-1.webp)

---

## Prompting Tips for 3D-Optimized Images
- Specify "front view" or "3/4 view" for the best 3D conversion angle.

- Add "white background" or "clean background" to reduce interference.

- Describe the complete form (don't just describe the head — describe the entire object).

- Avoid overly complex scenes — single subjects produce the best results.

---

## FAQ
### How do I generate an image from text in Meshy?

Open the Image module, go to AI Image Generation, enter a description, pick a style, generate, then send the result to Image to 3D.

### What's the difference between AI Image Generation and Text to 3D?

AI Image Generation creates a 2D image first for precise visual control before converting to 3D; Text to 3D goes directly from text to model.

### How do I write prompts for 3D-ready images?

Specify a front or 3/4 view, add white background, describe the full object, and keep it to a single subject.

### What image styles can Meshy generate?

Presets include Realistic, Anime, Chibi, and more, optimized for clean conversion into 3D.

### Can I send a generated image directly to Image to 3D?

Yes. Click Send to Image to 3D to move your chosen image straight into the 3D pipeline.

---

## Related Links
- [Image to 3D](/webapp/image-to-3d) — Convert generated images to 3D

- [Prompting Guide](/webapp/guides/prompting) — Master the art of writing effective prompts

- [3D Agent](/webapp/3d-agent) — Explore concepts through conversation before generating images

# My Models & Asset Management
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/platform/asset-management

# My Models & Asset Management

Organize, search, and version your 3D assets in Meshy My Models, uploading external meshes for post-processing and tracking every edit you make.

---

## TL;DR
- All generated models are saved in My Models, with support for search, filtering, and batch operations.

- Supports uploading external models for post-processing (AI Texturing, Remesh, etc.).

- Model version history is traceable: original generation → each post-processing step preserved as a version.

![Meshy My Assets view: browse and filter models by type, texture, and animation status, with batch selection and upload](https://cdn.meshy.ai/webapp-assets/doc/my-models-asset-management-p1-1.webp)

---

## FAQ
### Where are my generated models stored in Meshy?

All generated models are saved automatically in My Models, with search, filtering, and batch operations.

### Can I upload my own models to Meshy?

Yes. You can upload external meshes for post-processing like AI Texturing and Remesh.

### Can I see previous versions of a model?

Yes. Model version history is preserved — from the original generation through each post-processing step.

### How do I download multiple models at once?

Use batch operations in My Models to select and download several assets together.

### Why can't I download my model?

Make sure generation finished successfully and your plan allows download; check the model's status in My Models.

---

## Related Links
- [Text to 3D](/webapp/text-to-3d) — Generation includes initial textures
- [Image to 3D](/webapp/image-to-3d) — Single image workflow with detailed parameters
- [3D Agent](/webapp/3d-agent) — Conversational batch concept generation with style consistency

# Export & File Formats
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/platform/export-formats

# Export & File Formats

Meshy supports 6 major export formats — choosing the right one for your use case avoids the most common beginner mistakes.

---

## TL;DR
- Supports 6 major export formats: GLB, FBX, OBJ, STL, USDZ, 3MF.

- Each format is suited to different use cases — choosing the wrong format is one of the most common beginner mistakes.

- Texture packaging varies by format: GLB embeds textures, FBX/OBJ use separate files.

---

## Format Selection Guide
| I need to... | Use Format | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Display a 3D model on a web page | GLB | Web standard, embedded textures, small size |
| Import into Unity | FBX | Best native Unity support |
| Import into Unreal Engine | FBX | Best native Unreal support |
| Import into Blender | GLB/FBX | Both supported; GLB is more open |
| Apple AR Quick Look | USDZ | The only AR format for Apple ecosystem |
| 3D print (single color) | STL | All slicer software supports it |
| 3D print (color) | 3MF | Supports color and multi-material |
| Exchange with legacy DCC tools | OBJ | Widest compatibility, but limited features |

---

## FAQ
### What 3D file formats does Meshy export?

GLB, FBX, OBJ, STL, USDZ, and 3MF — covering games, AR, 3D printing, and DCC tools.

### Which format should I use for game engines?

FBX for Unity and Unreal; GLB is best for web and AR.

### Which format should I use for 3D printing?

STL for single-color prints and 3MF for color or multi-material prints, since both store print-ready geometry.

### How does Meshy handle textures in each format?

GLB embeds textures in one file, while FBX and OBJ use separate texture files you must keep together.

### Why does my model appear white (no textures) after import?

The textures likely weren't linked — reassign the texture maps in your engine, or use GLB, which embeds them automatically.

---

## Related Links
- [Quick Start](/webapp/getting-started) — Includes first export steps
- [Glossary](/webapp/glossary) — Format terminology explained

# Prompting Best Practices
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/prompting

# Prompting Best Practices

Prompt quality is the #1 factor affecting 3D generation results — learn the formula, goal-based tips, and good-versus-bad examples that consistently produce better generations.

---

## TL;DR
- Prompt quality is the #1 factor affecting 3D generation results.

- An effective prompt contains four elements: subject description + material/texture + art style + technical specs.

- Longer prompts aren't always better — key information placed first carries the highest weight.

- Meshy 6 has stronger prompt comprehension, supporting more complex descriptions.

- Different goals require different strategies: realistic vs stylized, game assets vs 3D printing.

---

## Prompt Structure Formula
```text
[Subject] + [Material/Texture] + [Art Style] + [Technical Constraints]
```

**Example**:

```text
A medieval knight's helmet          ← Subject
with scratched iron surface         ← Material
in dark fantasy art style           ← Style
low-poly, game-ready asset          ← Technical constraints
```

---

## Prompt Tips by Goal
**For Realistic Models**:

- Describe real materials: "brushed stainless steel", "oak wood with visible grain"

- Add detail layers: "main body → surface details → wear/aging"

- Avoid contradictory descriptions

**For Stylized / Cartoon Models**:

- Specify style keywords: "Pixar style", "Studio Ghibli", "flat shading cel-shaded"

- Emphasize shape language: "round", "exaggerated proportions", "chibi"

**For Game Assets (Low Poly)**:

- Explicitly specify "low-poly" or "game-ready"

- Avoid excessive detail descriptions

- Include "clean edges", "minimal geometry"

**For 3D Printing**:

- Emphasize structural integrity: "solid", "watertight", "no floating parts"

- Avoid extremely thin features

- Specify "printable proportions"

**For 3D Agent Conversations**:

- Be conversational — the agent understands context from your chat history

- Start broad ("I want to create cyberpunk props for a game") and let the agent help refine

- Request batch concepts: "Show me 6 variations of this idea"

- Reference earlier concepts: "I like the third one — can we make it more detailed?"

---

## Prompt Do's and Don'ts
| ✅ Do | ❌ Don't |
| --- | --- |
| "a wooden treasure chest with iron bands" | "a box" (too vague) |
| "front-facing, centered, white background" | "amazing beautiful epic" (empty adjectives) |
| "low-poly cartoon style, 5000 faces" | "make it look good" (not actionable) |
| "weathered stone surface with moss" | "stone and wood and metal and glass" (too many materials) |

---

## Negative Prompts
Use negative prompts to exclude unwanted elements:

- "no background elements"

- "without floating particles"

- "no text or labels"

---

## Examples: Good vs Bad
**Good Prompt**: "A sci-fi plasma rifle with glowing blue energy core, carbon fiber body with chrome accents, cyberpunk style, game-ready low-poly asset"

**Bad Prompt**: "cool gun"

**Good Prompt (3D Printing)**: "A chess rook piece, medieval castle tower design, solid structure, no thin overhangs, 8cm tall, printable without supports"

**Bad Prompt (3D Printing)**: "chess piece" (no structural guidance for printability)

---

## FAQ
### How do I write a good 3D generation prompt?

Use the formula Subject + Material/Texture + Art Style + Technical Constraints, and put the most important details first.

### Do longer prompts produce better 3D models?

Not necessarily. Clarity and key details placed first matter more than length — the earliest words carry the most weight.

### How do I prompt for low-poly game assets?

Explicitly include "low-poly" or "game-ready," add "clean edges" and "minimal geometry," and avoid heavy detail.

### How do I prompt for 3D-printable models?

Emphasize "solid," "watertight," and "no thin overhangs," avoid extremely thin features, and specify printable proportions.

### Can I use negative prompts in Meshy?

Yes. Exclude unwanted elements with phrases like "no background elements," "without floating particles," or "no text or labels."

---

## Related Links
- [3D Agent](/webapp/3d-agent) — Conversational prompting through chat
- [AI Texturing](/webapp/guides/3d-model/ai-texturing) — Style prompts for texture generation
- [AI Image Generation](/webapp/guides/image/ai-image-generation) — Prompting for 2D images

# Scene Compose

Arrange multiple 3D models into a complete scene composition using drag-and-drop placement, scaling, and rotation.

---

## TL;DR
- Arrange multiple 3D models into a complete scene composition.

- Supports drag-and-drop positioning, scaling, and rotation.

- Ideal for game level prototypes, architecture visualization, product showcase scenes.

---

## When to Use
- You have multiple individual 3D assets and want to compose them into a scene.

- Game level layout prototyping.

- Product scene displays (e.g., multiple items on a table).

---

## When NOT to Use
- You only need a single standalone object → Generate directly in the 3D Model module

- You need professional-grade scene editing → Export to Blender/Unity

---

## FAQ
### What is Scene Compose in Meshy?

It lets you arrange multiple 3D models into a complete scene using drag-and-drop placement, scaling, and rotation.

### What is Scene Compose best for?

Game level prototypes, architecture visualization, and product showcase scenes built from several assets.

### Can I generate a video from a composed scene?

Yes. Send your scene to AI Video Generation to produce a rendered showcase video.

### When should I not use Scene Compose?

For a single standalone object, generate it directly in the 3D Model module; for professional scene editing, export to Blender or Unity.

### Can I export a Scene Compose layout to a game engine?

Yes. Export the assets to DCC tools or game engines via Meshy's plugins for further editing.

# Texture Edit
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/texture-edit

# Texture Edit

Paint-based texture editing directly on your 3D model with real-time preview.

---

## TL;DR
- Paint-based texture editing directly on your 3D model with real-time preview.

- Use text prompts to generate or modify textures from any viewing angle.

- Smart Healing Tool for cleaning up imperfections on the fly.

- Full edit history with undo/redo support.

---

## When to Use
- You want to touch up or modify specific areas of an existing texture without regenerating the entire surface.

- AI Texturing produced a good overall result, but certain regions need refinement (e.g., a misplaced pattern, unwanted color bleed, seam artifacts).

- You need to add or change details on a specific part of the model (e.g., add battle damage to one shoulder, change the logo on a chest plate).

- You want to clean up small imperfections without leaving the Meshy workspace.

---

## When NOT to Use
- You need a complete texture overhaul → Use AI Texturing to regenerate the full PBR map set from a new prompt.

- You need to edit the geometry (mesh shape) → Use Remesh or edit in Blender.

---

## Key Features
| Feature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| AI Texture Edit | Draw a mask on the area you want to change, enter a text prompt describing the desired result, and generate. Works from any camera angle. |
| Smart Healing Tool | Select and paint over imperfections (seams, artifacts, color bleeds) while orbiting the model. Automatically fills and blends the repaired area. |
| History Control | Full undo/redo stack. Backtrack through any edit at any time. |

---

## Step-by-Step
1. Open a textured model in the editor.

2. Enter Texture Edit mode.

3. Orbit to the angle where you want to make changes.

4. To regenerate an area: Draw a mask over the target region → Enter a text prompt describing the desired look → Generate. Preview the result in real time.

5. To heal imperfections: Switch to the Smart Healing Tool → Paint over the artifact or seam → The tool auto-blends the area.

6. Repeat from different angles as needed. Use undo/redo to compare versions.

7. Confirm and save when satisfied.

<YouTube id="SZeBC_g_ARg" title="New Decal Tool is LIVE! | 3D Texture Editing Just Got Smarter" />

---

## Tips
- Work from multiple angles to ensure edits blend seamlessly across the UV seams.

- Use AI Texture Edit for creative changes (adding details, changing style) and Smart Healing for corrective fixes (removing artifacts, smoothing seams).

- Combine with AI Texturing for the best workflow: generate the base texture with AI Texturing, then refine specific areas with Texture Edit.

---

## FAQ
### How do I edit a 3D model's texture in Meshy?

Open a textured model, enter Texture Edit, orbit to the area, mask the region, and enter a prompt to regenerate it with real-time preview.

### Can I fix texture artifacts without regenerating everything?

Yes. The Smart Healing Tool blends out seams and imperfections on specific areas while leaving the rest untouched.

### When should I use Texture Edit vs AI Texturing?

Use Texture Edit for localized touch-ups and detail changes; use AI Texturing to regenerate the entire surface from a new prompt.

### Can I undo texture edits?

Yes. Texture Edit keeps a full edit history with undo/redo so you can compare and revert versions.

### Can I edit textures from any angle?

Yes. Orbit the model and paint or regenerate from multiple angles to keep edits seamless across UV seams.

---

## Related Links
- [Text to 3D](/webapp/text-to-3d) — Generation includes initial textures

- [Image to 3D](/webapp/image-to-3d) — Single image workflow with detailed parameters

- [3D Agent](/webapp/3d-agent) — Conversational batch concept generation with style consistency

# 3D Printing Workflow
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/use-cases/3d-printing

# 3D Printing Workflow

Generate 3D-print-ready models with Meshy, remesh for watertight geometry, and export STL or 3MF straight to your slicer.

---

## TL;DR
- Meshy can generate 3D-print-ready models, but proper post-processing is required.

- Key success factors: watertight mesh + adequate wall thickness + correct export format.

- Key steps: Generate → Check & Repair → Scale → Export STL/3MF → Slice → Print.

- Meshy is particularly suited for printing: miniatures/figurines, chess pieces, custom gifts, decorations, prototypes.

- 3D Agent provides a conversational workflow for makers who need help creating custom models.

- Meshy 6 produces better quality and topology than Meshy 5, making it more suitable for printing.

---

## End-to-End Workflow: From Idea to Print
1. **Generate**: Text to 3D (description + "solid, printable, no thin overhangs") or Image to 3D. Alternatively, use 3D Agent to brainstorm and create custom concepts.

2. **Check & Repair**: Run the built-in printability check to detect and fix common topology issues that cause 3D printing failures: non-manifold edges, degenerate faces, holes and open boundaries. Repair modifies geometry to ensure a watertight output.

3. **Scale**: Confirm model dimensions before export (Meshy uses cm as the unit).

4. **Export**: STL (single-color printing) or 3MF (color/multi-material printing).

5. **Slice**: Import into slicer software (OrcaSlicer, BambuStudio, etc.).

6. **Print**: Send to the 3D printer.

<YouTube id="y_wZVIUkiGI" title="AI Auto-Repair: Generate Print-Ready Models in One Click" />

---

## Design for Printability
**Minimum Wall Thickness**

| Print Technology | Min. Wall Thickness | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FDM | 1.2 mm | Depends on nozzle diameter |
| SLA/DLP | 0.5 mm | Better for fine details |
| SLS | 0.8 mm | No support needed |

**Overhang Guidelines**

- FDM: Overhangs exceeding 45° require support.

- SLA: More forgiving of overhangs, but still needs support points.

- SLS: No support needed — highest design freedom.

**Base & Stability**

- Add a base to character/figurine models.

- Base should be at least 3mm thick.

- You can specify "with a stable circular base" in your prompt or agent conversation.

---

## Troubleshooting for 3D Printing
| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Slicer reports "non-manifold" | Mesh has open edges/overlapping faces | Remesh or repair in Meshmixer |
| Breaks during printing | Connection points too thin | Thicken connection areas in a DCC tool |
| Bottom warping | Base too thin or poor bed adhesion | Thicken base, use brim/raft when printing |
| Detail loss | Print resolution insufficient | Use a higher-precision printer (SLA), or scale up the model |
| Color printing looks off | 3MF color mapping issues | Preview and adjust in slicer software |

---

## Export Format Guide for 3D Printing
| Format | Color | Best For | Slicer Compatibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| STL | ❌ | FDM/SLA single-color printing | All slicer software |
| 3MF | ✅ | Color printing, multi-material | Cura, PrusaSlicer, Bambu |
| OBJ | ⚠️ | Limited color support | Some slicer software |

---

## FAQ
### Can I 3D print models made with Meshy?

Yes. Generate your model, run the printability check, scale it, and export STL or 3MF for your slicer.

### What makes a Meshy model 3D-printable?

A watertight mesh, adequate wall thickness, and the correct export format (STL or 3MF).

### Should I export STL or 3MF for 3D printing?

Use STL for single-color printing and 3MF for color or multi-material printing.

### How do I fix a model that isn't watertight?

Run Meshy's built-in Check & Repair to fix non-manifold edges, degenerate faces, and holes for a watertight output.

### What wall thickness and base do figurines need?

Keep walls thick enough for your printer and material, and add a stable base at least ~3mm thick to figurines.

---

## Related Links
- [3D Agent](/webapp/3d-agent) — Brainstorm custom printing ideas through conversation
- [Glossary](/webapp/glossary) — What is watertight mesh

---

# Game Assets
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/guides/use-cases/game-assets

# Game Assets

Rapidly generate 3D assets for games — characters, props, environment objects, vehicles — and take them through the full pipeline to export.

---

## TL;DR
- Meshy can rapidly generate 3D assets for games: characters, props, environment objects, vehicles.

- Full pipeline: Generate → Remesh (optimize faces) → AI Texturing (PBR) → Rigging (characters) → Export (FBX/GLB).

- Best for: prototyping, indie game development, placeholder assets, concept exploration.

- 3D Agent excels at generating batches of style-consistent assets for a cohesive game world.

- Export formats: FBX (Unity/Unreal), GLB (Web/Three.js).

---

## End-to-End Workflow: Game Character
1. **Concept**: Use Text to 3D, Image to 3D, or 3D Agent to generate base character.

2. **Optimize**: Remesh to target polygon budget (e.g., mobile: 5K, PC: 20K).

3. **Texture**: AI Texturing with PBR maps (Albedo + Normal + Roughness + Metallic).

4. **Rig**: Auto-rig for humanoid skeleton.

5. **Animate**: Browse and apply from 500+ animation presets (walk & run, body movements, daily actions, fighting moves, and more).

6. **Export**: FBX for Unity/Unreal, or GLB for web.

<YouTube id="MUJp6wOqu6M" title="Meshy + Blender: How to Create 3D Characters in Dramatic Poses in MINUTES!" />

---

## End-to-End Workflow: Style-Consistent Asset Set with 3D Agent
1. **Start a conversation**: Describe your game's visual direction (e.g., "I'm building a cyberpunk RPG and need a set of props").

2. **Explore**: The agent suggests creative directions and generates batch visual concepts.

3. **Refine**: Select favorites, ask for variations, adjust style through conversation.

4. **Generate**: Turn selected concepts into 3D models.

5. **Post-process**: Remesh, texture, and export as needed.

<YouTube id="00tiy745MAc" title="Generate a Full Set of Game Assets in One Chat with Meshy 3D Agent" />

---

## Polygon Budget Reference
| Platform | Character | Prop | Environment Piece |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mobile (casual) | 3K–5K | 500–2K | 1K–5K |
| Mobile (AAA) | 10K–20K | 2K–5K | 5K–15K |
| PC/Console | 20K–50K | 5K–15K | 10K–50K |
| VR | 10K–30K | 2K–8K | 5K–20K |

---

## FAQ
### Can I use Meshy to make game assets?

Yes. Meshy generates characters, props, environment objects, and vehicles, then optimizes and rigs them for Unity and Unreal.

### What's the workflow for a game-ready character in Meshy?

Generate → Remesh to your polygon budget → AI Texturing (PBR) → Rigging → Animate → export FBX or GLB.

### What polygon budget should I target for games?

Roughly 5K for mobile and ~20K for PC; use Remesh to hit your target.

### Which export format should I use for Unity or Unreal?

FBX for Unity and Unreal; GLB for web and Three.js projects.

### How do I make a style-consistent set of game assets?

Use the 3D Agent to generate batches of concepts with a shared art direction, then convert them to 3D.

---

## Related Links
- [3D Agent](/webapp/3d-agent) — Style-consistent batch concept generation through chat
- [Remesh](/webapp/guides/3d-model/remesh) — Optimize for target polygon budget
- [Rigging](/webapp/guides/3d-model/rigging) — Character animation setup

# Bambu Studio
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/bambu-studio

# Bambu Studio

Learn how to use Meshy to send 3D models directly to Bambu Studio for 3D printing.

---

> **Note:** Meshy now supports Bambu Studio bridging directly from the workspace. Pro members and above can send models to Bambu Studio following the steps below.

## Overview

<span className="font-bold text-inherit">Meshy for Bambu Studio</span> is a seamless bridge integration that allows you to import <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI-generated models</span> directly into Bambu Studio. With this feature, you can effortlessly load and prepare 3D assets for printing, significantly enhancing your workflow efficiency.

## Sending Models to Bambu Studio

Navigate to the model you want in your <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI workspace</span>, click the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Print</span> menu, and select <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Send to Bambu Studio</span>.

   ![Meshy-SendToPrint](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/bambu-plugin/newpanel/doc_sendtoprint.webp)

   ![SendToBambu](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/bambu-plugin/newpanel/doc_sendtobambu.webp)

After a short loading period, a prompt window will pop up asking you to check <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Always allow www.meshy.ai to open links of this type in the associated app</span>, and then click the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Open BambuStudio</span> button.

   ![bambu-plugin-5](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/bambu-plugin/5.png)

Then the Bambu Studio software will be automatically opened.

After opening, select <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Yes</span> in the pop-up window.

   ![bambu-plugin-6](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/bambu-plugin/6.png)

If this is your first time using this feature, a window will pop up prompting you to select <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Don't show again</span> and click the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">OK</span> button.

   ![bambu-plugin-7](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/bambu-plugin/7.png)

Then, the model will be automatically downloaded and imported directly into your <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Bambu Studio</span>.

   ![bambu-plugin-8](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/bambu-plugin/8.png)

Any 3D model you generate in your workspace—regardless of the method used—can be effortlessly sent to Bambu Studio via the Print menu.

   ![MorePrint](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/bambu-plugin/newpanel/doc-moreprint.webp)

Likewise, models published by other users in the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI community</span> are fully supported and can also be seamlessly sent to Bambu Studio.

   ![Meshy-Community](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/bambu-plugin/newpanel/doc-community.webp)

---

# Elegoo Slicer
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/elegoo-slicer

# Elegoo Slicer

Learn how to use Meshy to send 3D models directly to Elegoo Slicer for 3D printing.

---

> **Note:** Meshy now supports Elegoo Slicer bridging directly from the workspace. Pro members and above can send models to Elegoo Slicer following the steps below.

## Overview

<span className="font-bold text-inherit">Meshy for Elegoo Slicer</span> is a seamless bridge integration that allows you to import <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI-generated models</span> directly into Elegoo Slicer. With this feature, you can effortlessly load and prepare 3D assets for printing, significantly enhancing your workflow efficiency.

## Sending Models to Elegoo Slicer

Navigate to the model you want in your <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI workspace</span>, click the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Print</span> menu, and select <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Send to Elegoo Slicer</span>.

   ![Meshy-SendToPrint](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/elegoo-plugin/doc_sendtoprint.webp)

   ![SendToElegoo](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/elegoo-plugin/doc_sendtoelegoo.webp)

After a short loading period, a prompt window will pop up asking you to check <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Always allow www.meshy.ai to open links of this type in the associated app</span>, and then click the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Open Elegoo Slicer</span> button.

   ![ElegooConfirm](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/elegoo-plugin/doc_elegoo_confirm.webp)

Then the Elegoo Slicer software will be automatically opened and start importing the model.

   ![ElegooLoading](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/elegoo-plugin/doc_elegoo_confirm2.webp)

After the loading is complete, select the imported model on the software's main interface, and click to enter.

   ![ElegooResult](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/elegoo-plugin/doc_elegoo_result.webp)

Any 3D model you generate in your workspace—regardless of the method used—can be effortlessly sent to Elegoo Slicer via the Print menu.

   ![MorePrint](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/elegoo-plugin/doc_moreprint.webp)

Likewise, models published by other users in the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI community</span> are fully supported and can also be seamlessly sent to Elegoo Slicer.

   ![Meshy-Community](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/elegoo-plugin/doc-community.webp)

# Flash Studio

Learn how to use Meshy to send 3D models directly to Flash Studio for 3D printing.

---

> **Note:** Meshy now supports Flash Studio bridging directly from the workspace. Pro members and above can send models to Flash Studio following the steps below.

## Overview

<span className="font-bold text-inherit">Meshy for Flash Studio</span> is a seamless bridge integration that lets you import <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI-generated models</span> directly into Flash Studio — Flashforge's official slicer. With this feature, you can effortlessly load and prepare 3D assets for printing, significantly enhancing your workflow efficiency.

## Sending Models to Flash Studio

### 1. Open the Print menu

From the model you want in your <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI workspace</span>, click the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Print</span> menu and select <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Send to Flash Studio</span>.

   ![flash-studio-send-to-entry](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/flash-studio/01-send-to-entry.webp)

### 2. Confirm the browser prompt

After a short loading period, the browser will pop up asking you to allow www.meshy.ai to open links of this type in the associated app. Tick <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Always allow</span> if you don't want to be asked again, then click <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Open Flash Studio</span>.

   ![flash-studio-browser-prompt](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/flash-studio/02-browser-prompt.webp)

### 3. Model loads in Flash Studio

Flash Studio will launch automatically and your model will be downloaded and imported into the workspace — ready to slice and print.

   ![flash-studio-loaded](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/flash-studio/03-loaded.webp)

## More Ways to Send

Any 3D model you generate in your workspace — and any community-published model — can be sent to Flash Studio from multiple surfaces:

- From a model's <span className="font-bold text-inherit">overview page</span>, use the entry in the action bar.

   ![flash-studio-overview-entry](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/flash-studio/04-overview-entry.webp)

- From the model's dedicated <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Print panel</span>, pick Flash Studio in the printer grid.

   ![flash-studio-print-panel](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/flash-studio/05-print-panel-entry.webp)

Likewise, models published by other users in the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI community</span> are fully supported and can also be seamlessly sent to Flash Studio.

   ![flashstudio-community](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/flash-studio/doc-community.webp)

# Meshy 3D Printing Platforms Documentation
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/introduction

# Meshy 3D Printing Platforms Documentation

Meshy supports seamless integration with popular 3D printing slicer software, allowing you to send models directly from your workspace to your preferred printing application.

---

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Welcome to the 3D Printing Platforms Documentation!</span>
>
> In this section, you'll learn how to send your MeshyAI-generated 3D models directly to various 3D printing slicer software with just a few clicks.
>
> Let's get started! 🚀

## Overview

Meshy's 3D Printing integration allows Pro members and above to send models directly from the MeshyAI workspace to supported slicer applications. Simply click the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Print</span> menu in your workspace and select your preferred slicer software.

The model will be automatically downloaded and imported into the selected application, ready for slicing and printing.

## Supported Platforms

Currently, Meshy supports the following 3D printing slicer software:

- **[Flash Studio](/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/flash-studio)** - Official slicer for Flashforge 3D printers
- **[Snapmaker Orca](/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/snapmaker)** - Official slicer for Snapmaker 3D printers
- **[Bambu Studio](/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/bambu-studio)** - Official slicer for Bambu Lab 3D printers
- **[OrcaSlicer](/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/orcaslicer)** - Open-source slicer based on Bambu Studio
- **[Creality Print](/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/creality-print)** - Official slicer for Creality 3D printers
- **[Elegoo Slicer](/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/elegoo-slicer)** - Official slicer for Elegoo 3D printers
- **[Ultimaker Cura](/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/ultimaker-cura)** - Official slicer for Ultimaker 3D printers
- **[Lychee Slicer](/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/lychee-slicer)** - Professional slicer by Mango3D for 3D printers

Each platform guide includes step-by-step instructions for sending models from Meshy to that specific slicer application.

---

# Lychee Slicer
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/3d-printing-platforms/lychee-slicer

# Lychee Slicer

Learn how to use Meshy to send 3D models directly to Lychee Slicer for 3D printing.

---

> **Note:** Meshy now supports Lychee Slicer bridging directly from the workspace. Pro members and above can send models to Lychee Slicer following the steps below.

## Overview

<span className="font-bold text-inherit">Meshy for Lychee Slicer</span> is a seamless bridge integration that allows you to import <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI-generated models</span> directly into Lychee Slicer by Mango3D. With this feature, you can effortlessly load and prepare 3D assets for printing, significantly enhancing your workflow efficiency.

## Sending Models to Lychee Slicer

Navigate to the model you want in your <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI workspace</span>, click the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Print</span> menu, and select <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Send to Lychee Slicer</span>.

   ![Meshy-SendToPrint](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/lychee-plugin/doc_sendtoprint.webp)

   ![SendToLychee](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/lychee-plugin/doc_sendtolychee.webp)

After a short loading period, a prompt window will pop up asking you to check <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Always allow www.meshy.ai to open links of this type in the associated app</span>, and then click the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Open Lychee Slicer</span> button.

   ![LycheeConfirm](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/lychee-plugin/doc_confirm.webp)

Then the Lychee Slicer application will open and display a dialog asking you to enter a filename for the model.

> **Note:** Please be sure to add the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">.3mf</span> suffix to the filename. Without the correct file extension, the model will fail to load after downloading.
>
>    ![LycheeSaveDialog](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/lychee-plugin/doc_confirm1.webp)

After entering the filename with the .3mf extension and confirming, the model will be imported into Lychee Slicer.

   ![LycheeResult](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/lychee-plugin/doc_lychee_result.webp)

Any 3D model you generate in your workspace—regardless of the method used—can be effortlessly sent to Lychee Slicer via the Print menu.

   ![MorePrint](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/lychee-plugin/doc_moreprint.webp)

Likewise, models published by other users in the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI community</span> are fully supported and can also be seamlessly sent to Lychee Slicer.

   ![Meshy-Community](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/lychee-plugin/doc-community.webp)

# Meshy for 3dsMax
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/3dsmax/introduction

# Meshy for 3dsMax

This is the official documentation of Meshy 3dsMax plugin, you'll find detailed instructions on how to use this plugin to import models you generated in Meshy, and create your own textures by Meshy in the 3dsMax editor.

---

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Welcome to the Meshy 3dsMax Plugin Documentation!</span>
>
> In this guide, we will walk you through how to efficiently use this plugin. Learn how to send a model from the official website to a scene with one click.
>
> Let's get started! 🚀

## Overview

<span className="font-bold text-inherit">Meshy 3dsMax Plugin</span> is a 3dsMax plugin that enables seamless import of <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI-generated models.</span> With this plugin, you can effortlessly load and edit 3D assets, significantly enhancing your workflow efficiency.

## Installation

Download the plugin from the <ExternalLink href={"https://www.meshy.ai/integrations/3ds-max"}>Meshy for 3ds Max integration page</ExternalLink>, where you can grab the latest build for your platform.

After downloading the plug-in resource, unzip it and place it in any local location.
Open 3ds Max, find <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Scripting</span> in the top bar, then click <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Run Script</span> and select the plugin code you just extracted.
   ![3dsMax-plugin-1](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/3dsMax-plugin/2.PNG)

Then, the plugin window will pop up.
   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/3dsMax-plugin/3.PNG" alt="3dsMax-plugin-3" width="300px" style={{width: "500px", height: "auto"}} />

# Bridge to Blender
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/blender/bridge-to-blender

# Bridge to Blender

This guide shows you how to use the Bridge to Blender feature to automatically import Meshy assets into your Blender workspace. The Bridge creates a seamless connection between MeshyAI and Blender, allowing you to transfer 3D models with a single click.

---

> **Note:** Before you begin, make sure you have downloaded and installed the Meshy for Blender plugin. For detailed instructions, please refer to the [Introduction](/webapp/plugins/blender/introduction) section.

> **Note:** Meshy now supports Blender bridging directly from the workspace. Pro members and above can send models to Blender following the steps below.

## Run Bridge in Meshy-Blender Plugin

Open the Meshy Blender Plugin within Blender. The first feature listed is Meshy Bridge. Click <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Run Bridge</span> to initialize and start the bridge connection.

When the bridge is running, the button will change to <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Bridge ON</span> and remain highlighted, indicating that the local server is active and ready to receive model transfers from MeshyAI.

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/2.png" alt="bridge-to-blender-1" width="300px" style={{width: "500px", height: "auto"}} />

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Bridge Status</span>
>
> The Bridge runs a local HTTP server on port 5324. Make sure this port is not blocked by your firewall or used by another application. When the bridge is active, it will automatically process incoming model transfers and import them into your current Blender scene.

## Sending Models to Blender

Navigate to the model you want in your <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI workspace</span>, click the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">DCC Bridge</span> menu, and select <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Send to Blender</span>.

   ![Meshy-SendToDCC](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055-newpanel/doc_sendtodcc.webp)

   ![SendToBlender](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055-newpanel/doc_sendtoblender.webp)

The model will be automatically downloaded and imported directly into your Blender scene. The plugin handles the entire process seamlessly:

- Downloads the model file from MeshyAI
- Detects the file format (GLB or ZIP)
- Imports the model into your scene
- Applies automatic optimizations (merging duplicate vertices, setting up materials)
- Preserves model names and structure

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v052/29.webp" alt="bridge-to-blender-9" width="800px" style={{width: "800px", height: "auto"}} />

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Can't see the materials/textures?</span>
>
> If an imported model appears plain gray in the viewport, it's usually because Blender's viewport is in <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Solid</span> shading mode — this mode doesn't render textures, and it does not mean the import failed. Hover your mouse over the 3D viewport and press <span className="font-bold text-inherit">`Z`</span> (or use the shading mode buttons in the top-right corner of the viewport), then switch to <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Material Preview</span> to see the full materials.
>
> <img src="/images/blender-plugin/material-preview-z.png" alt="switch-to-material-preview" width="800px" style={{width: "800px", height: "auto"}} />

Any 3D model you generate in your workspace—regardless of the method used—can be effortlessly imported into <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Blender</span> via the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">DCC Bridge</span>.

   ![MoreDCC](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055-newpanel/doc-moredcc.webp)

Likewise, models published by other users in the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI community</span> are fully supported and can also be seamlessly imported into Blender using the DCC Bridge integration.

   ![Meshy-Community](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055-newpanel/doc-community.webp)

## How Bridge Works

The Bridge to Blender feature establishes a local HTTP server within Blender that communicates with MeshyAI's web interface. Here's what happens during the transfer process:

1. **Connection**: When you click the Blender icon on MeshyAI, the website sends a POST request to your local Blender instance at `localhost:5324`.

2. **Download**: The plugin receives the model URL and automatically downloads the file to a temporary location.

3. **Format Detection**: The plugin automatically detects whether the file is a GLB file or a ZIP archive containing GLB files.

4. **Import**: The model is imported into Blender using the GLTF importer, with automatic optimizations applied:
   - Duplicate vertices are merged
   - Materials are automatically set up
   - Color attributes are preserved and connected to materials
   - Model names are prefixed with "Meshy_" for easy identification

5. **Cleanup**: Temporary files are automatically removed after import.

The entire process happens in the background, allowing you to continue working while models are being imported.

## Supported File Formats

The Bridge to Blender feature supports the following file formats:

- **GLB files**: Direct import of GLB (GL Transmission Format Binary) files
- **ZIP archives**: Automatic extraction and import of GLB files contained within ZIP archives

When importing models, the plugin automatically:
- Handles bone hierarchies and animations (if present)
- Preserves texture mappings and material properties
- Maintains vertex color attributes
- Applies appropriate scaling and transformations

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Model Processing</span>
>
> Imported models are automatically optimized for use in Blender. The plugin merges duplicate vertices, sets up materials to display color attributes, and ensures proper naming conventions. If a model lacks materials, a default material with color attribute support will be created automatically.

---

## Plugin Features
The Meshy Blender plugin provides a comprehensive suite of tools for working with 3D models, especially for preparing models for 3D printing. Here's an overview of the main features:

### Bridge to Blender

The Bridge feature creates a seamless connection between MeshyAI and Blender, allowing you to transfer 3D models with a single click. Once enabled, you can import models directly from the MeshyAI website into your Blender scene without manual downloads.

**Key Features:**
- One-click model import from MeshyAI
- Automatic format detection (GLB, ZIP)
- Automatic model optimization
- Preserves materials and color attributes

Learn more: [Bridge to Blender](/webapp/plugins/blender/bridge-to-blender)

### Model Analysis

The Analyze panel provides comprehensive tools to check your 3D models for issues before printing. It includes statistical measurements and multiple geometry checks designed specifically for 3D printing preparation.

**Key Features:**
- Volume and area calculations
- Solid/watertight checks
- Self-intersection detection
- Thickness analysis
- Overhang detection
- Small pieces detection
- One-click "Check All" function

Learn more: [Model Analysis](/webapp/plugins/blender/model-analysis)

### Model Cleanup

The Clean Up panel offers automated tools to fix common geometry problems. These tools are essential for ensuring your models are print-ready.

**Key Features:**
- Make Manifold: Automatically repair non-manifold geometry
- Delete Small Pieces: Remove scattered fragments
- Automatic hole filling
- Normal direction correction

Learn more: [Model Cleanup](/webapp/plugins/blender/model-cleanup)

### Model Editing

The Edit panel provides tools to modify and prepare your models for printing, including size adjustments and orientation tools.

**Key Features:**
- Hollow: Create offset surfaces for hollow models
- Align XY: Rotate models to sit flat on the print bed
- Scale to Volume: Scale models to specific volumes
- Scale to Bounds: Scale models to fit within dimensions

Learn more: [Model Editing](/webapp/plugins/blender/model-editing)

### Model Export

The Export panel allows you to export your cleaned and prepared models in various formats suitable for 3D printing and sharing.

**Key Features:**
- Multiple format support (STL, OBJ, PLY)
- Export options (UVs, normals, colors)
- Texture copying
- Scene scale application

Learn more: [Model Export](/webapp/plugins/blender/model-export)

---

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Workflow Recommendation</span>
>
> For best results when preparing models for 3D printing:
> 1. Use **Bridge to Blender** to import models from MeshyAI
> 2. Run **Model Analysis** to check for issues
> 3. Use **Model Cleanup** to fix problems automatically
> 4. Use **Model Editing** to adjust size and orientation
> 5. Run analysis again to verify fixes
> 6. **Export** your model in STL format for printing
