# Model Analysis
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/blender/model-analysis

# Model Analysis

The Analyze panel provides comprehensive tools to check your 3D models for issues, making it perfect for preparing models for 3D printing. Use these tools to identify and fix problems before exporting.

---

> **Note:** Before you begin, make sure you have downloaded and installed the Meshy for Blender plugin. For detailed instructions, please refer to the [Introduction](/webapp/plugins/blender/introduction) section.

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Getting Started</span>
>
> To use the Analyze panel:
> 1. Select your 3D model in Blender
> 2. Open the Meshy panel in the sidebar (press `N` if hidden)
> 3. Expand the "Analyze" section
> 4. Click any check button to analyze your model

The Analyze panel is located in the Meshy category of Blender's sidebar. Here's what it looks like:

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/analyze-panel.png" alt="Analyze panel interface showing statistics and geometry check buttons" width="800px" style={{width: "800px", height: "auto"}} />

## Statistics

The Statistics section provides basic measurements of your model:

### Volume

Calculates the total volume of your mesh. This is useful for:
- Estimating material usage for 3D printing
- Comparing model sizes
- Ensuring models meet size requirements

Click <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Volume</span> to calculate and display the volume in your scene's unit system.

### Area

Calculates the total surface area of your mesh. This helps with:
- Estimating paint or coating requirements
- Understanding model complexity
- Surface finish planning

Click <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Area</span> to calculate and display the surface area.

## Geometry Checks

The Analyze panel includes multiple checks designed to identify common 3D printing issues:

### Solid

Checks if your model is a watertight solid with proper geometry:

- **Non-manifold Edges**: Edges that are shared by more than two faces, indicating holes or improperly connected geometry
- **Bad Contiguous Edges**: Edges where face directions are inconsistent (faces pointing inward vs. outward)

A model must be manifold (watertight) for successful 3D printing. Non-manifold geometry will cause slicing software to fail.

### Intersections

Detects self-intersecting faces where the model intersects itself. Self-intersections cause:
- 3D printing failures
- Incorrect geometry calculations
- Slicing errors

This check identifies all intersecting faces so you can fix them manually.

### Degenerate

Finds broken or invalid geometry:

- **Zero-Area Faces**: Faces that are too small (below the threshold)
- **Zero-Length Edges**: Edges where vertices overlap

You can adjust the threshold using the value field next to the button. The default threshold is 0.01 cm (0.1 mm).

### Non-Planar

Identifies faces that are not flat. Non-planar faces can cause:
- Rendering artifacts
- 3D printing issues
- Geometry errors

Adjust the angle threshold to control sensitivity. The default is 5 degrees.

### Thickness

Checks for walls that are too thin. Thin walls may:
- Break during printing
- Fail to print at all
- Create weak structures

Set the minimum thickness threshold (default: 1mm). Any faces thinner than this will be flagged.

### Sharp

Detects edges that are sharper than a specified angle. Very sharp edges:
- Are difficult to print accurately
- May require support material
- Can cause print failures

Adjust the angle threshold (default: 160 degrees) to control what's considered "sharp."

### Overhang

Identifies faces that overhang past a specified angle. Large overhangs:
- Require support material when 3D printing
- May fail to print without support
- Can cause print quality issues

Set the overhang angle threshold (default: 45 degrees) to identify problematic areas.

### Small Pieces

Detects small disconnected pieces in your model, similar to Houdini Labs' Delete Small tool. This is particularly useful for:
- Cleaning up photogrammetry scans
- Removing fragments from fluid simulations
- Finding scattered droplets or debris

**Detection Modes:**
- **Volume**: Detects by bounding box volume (units: cm³)
- **Area**: Detects by surface area (units: cm²)
- **Diagonal**: Detects by bounding box diagonal length (units: cm)

Set the size threshold and mode, then click <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Small Pieces</span> to find fragments below the threshold.

## Using Analysis Results

After running any check, results appear in the Results section at the bottom of the Analyze panel:

1. **View Results**: Each check displays the number of issues found
2. **Select Problem Areas**: Click on any result item to automatically select the problematic geometry in Edit Mode
3. **Clear Results**: Click the X button to clear all results

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/analyze-results.png" alt="Analysis results panel showing check results with issue counts" width="800px" style={{width: "800px", height: "auto"}} />

When you click a result item:
- Blender switches to Edit Mode (if not already)
- The problematic vertices, edges, or faces are selected
- You can then manually fix or delete the selected geometry

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/analyze-selected-geometry.png" alt="3D viewport showing selected problematic geometry highlighted in Edit Mode" width="800px" style={{width: "800px", height: "auto"}} />

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Edit Mode Required</span>
>
> To select and fix issues, you need to be in Edit Mode. The plugin will automatically switch to Edit Mode when you click on a result item, but you can also press `Tab` to toggle Edit Mode manually.

## Check All

Instead of running checks individually, you can run all checks at once:

Click <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Check All</span> to execute all geometry checks simultaneously. This is useful for:
- Quick model validation before printing
- Comprehensive quality checks
- Identifying multiple issues at once

All results will appear in the Results section, and you can click on any item to select and fix the corresponding geometry.

---

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Workflow Tip</span>
>
> For best results when preparing models for 3D printing:
> 1. Run "Check All" first to see all issues
> 2. Use the Clean Up panel to fix common problems automatically
> 3. Run checks again to verify fixes
> 4. Manually fix any remaining issues
> 5. Export your model when all checks pass

---

# Model Cleanup
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/blender/model-cleanup

# Model Cleanup

The Clean Up panel provides automated tools to fix common 3D model issues. These tools are essential for preparing models for 3D printing and ensuring they meet quality standards.

---

> **Note:** Before you begin, make sure you have downloaded and installed the Meshy for Blender plugin. For detailed instructions, please refer to the [Introduction](/webapp/plugins/blender/introduction) section.

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Before Cleaning</span>
>
> It's recommended to run checks from the Analyze panel first to identify issues. Then use the Clean Up tools to fix them automatically. After cleaning, run checks again to verify the fixes.

## Make Manifold

The <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Make Manifold</span> tool automatically repairs your model to make it watertight and print-ready. This is one of the most important steps in preparing a model for 3D printing.

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/cleanup-panel.png" alt="Clean Up panel interface showing Make Manifold button and Delete Small Pieces section" width="800px" style={{width: "800px", height: "auto"}} />

### What It Does

The Make Manifold tool performs several automated repairs:

1. **Deletes Loose Geometry**: Removes isolated vertices, edges, and faces that aren't connected to the main mesh
2. **Removes Interior Faces**: Deletes faces that are inside the model and not visible
3. **Merges Duplicate Vertices**: Combines vertices that are too close together (within the merge distance threshold)
4. **Fills Holes**: Automatically fills gaps and holes in the mesh
5. **Fixes Non-Manifold Geometry**: Resolves non-manifold edges and vertices
6. **Makes Normals Consistent**: Ensures all faces point outward for proper rendering and printing

### How to Use

1. Select your model in Object Mode
2. Open the Meshy panel and expand the "Clean Up" section
3. Click <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Make Manifold</span>
4. The tool will process your model and display a report showing what was modified

### Results

After running Make Manifold, you'll see a report showing:
- How many vertices were added or removed
- How many edges were added or removed
- How many faces were added or removed

This helps you understand what changes were made to your model.

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/cleanup-results.png" alt="Make Manifold operation report showing modified vertex, edge, and face counts" width="600px" style={{width: "600px", height: "auto"}} />

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Important</span>
>
> Make Manifold may modify your model's geometry. It's recommended to:
> - Save your work before running it
> - Check the results visually
> - Run Analyze checks again after cleaning to verify the fixes

## Delete Small Pieces

The <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Delete Small Pieces</span> tool removes small disconnected fragments from your model. This is particularly useful for cleaning up:
- Photogrammetry scans with scattered debris
- Fluid simulation meshes with droplets
- Models with unwanted fragments

### Detection Modes

You can choose how to measure piece size:

- **Volume**: Detects by bounding box volume (units: cm³)
  - Best for removing small solid fragments
  - Default threshold: 1.0 cm³

- **Area**: Detects by surface area (units: cm²)
  - Best for removing thin flakes or sheets
  - Useful for surface-based cleanup

- **Diagonal**: Detects by bounding box diagonal length (units: cm)
  - Best for removing fragments of any shape
  - Good general-purpose option

### How to Use

1. Select your model
2. In the Clean Up panel, find the "Delete Small Pieces" section
3. Choose your detection mode (Volume, Area, or Diagonal)
4. Set the size threshold (default: 1.0)
5. Click <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Delete Small Pieces</span>

### Tips

- **Preview First**: Use the Analyze panel's "Small Pieces" check to preview what will be deleted before actually deleting
- **Start Conservative**: Begin with a smaller threshold and increase if needed
- **Check Results**: After deletion, visually inspect your model to ensure important parts weren't removed

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Workflow Recommendation</span>
>
> Before deleting small pieces:
> 1. Run "Small Pieces" check in the Analyze panel to see what will be detected
> 2. Adjust the threshold if needed
> 3. Then use Delete Small Pieces to remove them

## Cleanup Workflow

For best results when cleaning models, follow this workflow:

### Step 1: Analyze

1. Select your model
2. Open the Analyze panel
3. Click <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Check All</span> to identify all issues
4. Review the results to understand what needs fixing

### Step 2: Clean Up

1. Switch to the Clean Up panel
2. Click <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Make Manifold</span> to fix basic geometry issues
3. If you have small fragments, use <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Delete Small Pieces</span> to remove them

### Step 3: Verify

1. Return to the Analyze panel
2. Run <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Check All</span> again
3. Verify that issues have been resolved
4. Manually fix any remaining issues if needed

### Step 4: Export

Once all checks pass, your model is ready to export using the Export panel.

---

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">3D Printing Preparation</span>
>
> For 3D printing, a model must be:
> - Manifold (watertight)
> - Free of self-intersections
> - Properly scaled
> - Have adequate wall thickness
>
> The Clean Up tools help ensure your model meets these requirements. Always verify with Analyze checks before printing.

---

# Model Editing
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/blender/model-editing

# Model Editing

The Edit panel provides tools to modify and prepare your models for 3D printing. These tools help you optimize models for printing, adjust orientation, and control size.

---

> **Note:** Before you begin, make sure you have downloaded and installed the Meshy for Blender plugin. For detailed instructions, please refer to the [Introduction](/webapp/plugins/blender/introduction) section.

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Editing Tools</span>
>
> All editing operations can be undone using Blender's undo system (Ctrl+Z / Cmd+Z). Make sure to save your work before making significant changes.

## Hollow

The <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Hollow</span> tool creates an offset surface, making a solid model hollow. This is useful for:
- Reducing material usage in 3D printing
- Creating shells for casting
- Making models lighter
- Creating containers or vases

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/edit-panel.png" alt="Edit panel interface showing Hollow, Align XY, and Scale To buttons" width="800px" style={{width: "800px", height: "auto"}} />

### Parameters

When you click Hollow, a dialog appears with these options:

- **Offset Direction**: Choose whether to offset inward or outward
  - **Inside**: Creates a shell inside the original model (most common)
  - **Outside**: Creates a shell outside the original model

- **Offset**: The thickness of the shell wall (default: 1.0 units)
  - Larger values create thicker walls
  - Must be less than half the model's thickness

- **Voxel Size**: The resolution of the voxel grid used for calculation
  - Smaller values preserve more detail but process slower
  - Default: 1.0 units
  - Lower values (0.1-0.5) for fine details
  - Higher values (1.0-2.0) for faster processing

- **Hollow Duplicate**: Creates a hollowed copy while keeping the original
  - If enabled, both original and hollow versions are kept
  - If disabled, only the hollow version remains

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/hollow-dialog.png" alt="Hollow tool dialog showing Offset Direction, Offset, Voxel Size, and Hollow Duplicate options" width="500px" style={{width: "500px", height: "auto"}} />

### How to Use

1. Select your model
2. Click <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Hollow</span> in the Edit panel
3. Adjust parameters in the dialog
4. Click OK to create the hollow model

### Tips

- **Check Thickness First**: Use the Analyze panel's Thickness check to ensure your model has adequate wall thickness before hollowing
- **Start Conservative**: Begin with smaller offset values and increase if needed
- **Voxel Size**: Use smaller voxel sizes for models with fine details
- **Test First**: Try hollowing on a copy of your model first

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Important</span>
>
> The hollow tool requires a closed, watertight mesh. Make sure your model is manifold (use Make Manifold in the Clean Up panel first). If the offset is too large relative to the model thickness, the operation may fail.

## Align XY

The <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Align XY</span> tool rotates your model so that selected faces lie parallel to the XY plane (ground plane). This is essential for:
- Ensuring models sit flat on the print bed
- Proper orientation for 3D printing
- Aligning models to a specific plane

### How to Use

1. Select your model
2. Enter Edit Mode (press `Tab`)
3. Select the faces you want to align to the ground (typically the bottom faces)
4. Click <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Align XY</span>

The model will automatically rotate so the selected faces are parallel to the XY plane.

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/align-xy-before-after.png" alt="Before and after comparison showing model rotation to align with XY plane" width="800px" style={{width: "800px", height: "auto"}} />

### Options

- **Weight by Face Area**: When enabled, larger faces have more influence on the rotation calculation
  - Recommended for models with varying face sizes
  - Provides more stable results

### Tips

- **Select Bottom Faces**: Select the faces that should touch the print bed
- **Multiple Objects**: You can align multiple objects at once by selecting them all
- **Check Orientation**: After aligning, verify the model orientation is correct

## Scale to Volume

The <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Scale to Volume</span> tool scales your model to a specific volume. This is useful for:
- Ensuring models meet size requirements
- Matching volumes between different models
- Preparing models for specific material quantities

### How to Use

1. Select your model(s)
2. Click <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Scale to Volume</span>
3. A dialog appears showing the current volume
4. Enter your desired volume
5. Click OK to scale

The model will be scaled proportionally to match the target volume.

### Tips

- **Current Volume**: The dialog shows the current volume, which you can use as a reference
- **Proportional Scaling**: The model scales uniformly in all directions
- **Multiple Objects**: If multiple objects are selected, their combined volume is used

## Scale to Bounds

The <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Scale to Bounds</span> tool scales your model to fit within a maximum length along its longest axis. This is useful for:
- Ensuring models fit within print bed dimensions
- Meeting size constraints
- Standardizing model sizes

### How to Use

1. Select your model(s)
2. Click <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Scale to Bounds</span>
3. A dialog appears showing the current longest dimension
4. Enter your desired maximum length
5. Click OK to scale

The model will be scaled so its longest dimension matches the target length.

### Tips

- **Longest Axis**: The tool automatically identifies and scales based on the longest axis
- **Proportional**: The model maintains its proportions
- **Print Bed Size**: Use your printer's bed dimensions as a reference

---

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">3D Printing Workflow</span>
>
> A typical workflow for preparing models:
> 1. **Analyze** - Check for issues
> 2. **Clean Up** - Fix geometry problems
> 3. **Edit** - Adjust size and orientation (Scale to Bounds, Align XY)
> 4. **Hollow** (optional) - Reduce material usage
> 5. **Analyze Again** - Verify everything is correct
> 6. **Export** - Save in STL format for printing

---

# Model Export
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/blender/model-export

# Model Export

The Export panel provides tools to export your models in various formats suitable for 3D printing, sharing, and further processing. Export your cleaned and prepared models with full control over format and options.

---

> **Note:** Before you begin, make sure you have downloaded and installed the Meshy for Blender plugin. For detailed instructions, please refer to the [Introduction](/webapp/plugins/blender/introduction) section.

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Before Exporting</span>
>
> Make sure your model is ready:
> - Run Analyze checks to verify geometry
> - Use Clean Up tools to fix issues
> - Adjust size and orientation in the Edit panel
> - Only then proceed to export

## Supported Formats

The Export panel supports three common 3D file formats:

### STL (Stereolithography)

**Best for**: 3D printing

- Most widely supported format for 3D printing
- Simple format containing only geometry (no colors, materials, or textures)
- Binary format is smaller and faster to process
- ASCII format is human-readable but larger

**Use STL when**:
- Exporting for 3D printing
- Sending to slicing software (Cura, PrusaSlicer, etc.)
- Maximum compatibility is needed

### OBJ (Wavefront OBJ)

**Best for**: General 3D modeling and sharing

- Universal format supported by most 3D software
- Supports materials and textures
- Can include UV coordinates and normals
- Text-based format

**Use OBJ when**:
- Sharing models with others
- Importing into other 3D software
- You need material/texture information

### PLY (Polygon File Format)

**Best for**: Models with vertex colors

- Supports vertex colors
- Can include UV coordinates and normals
- Good for scanned models with color data
- Binary or ASCII format

**Use PLY when**:
- Your model has vertex colors
- Working with scanned/photogrammetry data
- Color information is important

## Export Settings

The Export panel provides all the settings you need to export your models:

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/export-panel.png" alt="Export panel interface showing export path, format selection, and Export button" width="800px" style={{width: "800px", height: "auto"}} />

### Export Path

Set where to save the exported file:

- **Relative Path**: Use `//` to save relative to the Blender file location
- **Absolute Path**: Specify a full file path
- **Default**: If no path is set and the file isn't saved, exports go to your home directory

### Format Selection

Choose your export format from the dropdown:
- STL
- OBJ
- PLY

The format determines which options are available.

## Export Options

Expand the Options panel to access advanced settings:

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/blender-plugin/blender-plugin-v055/export-options.png" alt="Expanded Export Options panel showing General, Geometry, and Material options" width="800px" style={{width: "800px", height: "auto"}} />

### General Options

- **ASCII Format**: Save as text format instead of binary
  - Available for STL and PLY formats
  - Larger file size but human-readable
  - Useful for debugging or manual editing

- **Scene Scale**: Apply Blender's unit scale to the export
  - Ensures correct size in other software
  - Important for accurate 3D printing

### Geometry Options

Available for OBJ and PLY formats (STL only contains geometry):

- **UVs**: Export texture coordinates
  - Required if you want to use textures in other software
  - Preserves UV mapping information

- **Normals**: Export vertex normals
  - Improves shading in other software
  - Calculated if not explicitly set

- **Colors**: Export vertex color attributes
  - Preserves color information from vertex colors
  - Useful for scanned models with color data

### Material Options

- **Copy Textures**: Copy texture image files to the export location
  - Keeps textures with the exported model
  - Useful when sharing models with textures
  - Textures are copied to the same directory as the exported file

## Export Workflow

Follow these steps for successful exports:

### Step 1: Prepare Your Model

1. **Analyze**: Run checks to identify issues
2. **Clean Up**: Fix geometry problems
3. **Edit**: Adjust size and orientation
4. **Verify**: Run checks again to ensure everything is correct

### Step 2: Configure Export

1. **Select Objects**: Select the objects you want to export
2. **Choose Format**: Select STL for 3D printing, OBJ/PLY for other uses
3. **Set Path**: Choose where to save the file
4. **Adjust Options**: Expand Options panel and configure as needed

### Step 3: Export

1. Click the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Export</span> button
2. If the path wasn't set, a file browser will appear
3. Choose the save location and filename
4. The export will complete automatically

### Step 4: Verify

1. Check the export location for your file
2. Import into your target software to verify
3. For 3D printing, load into slicing software to check

---

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">3D Printing Export Tips</span>
>
> For best 3D printing results:
> - **Format**: Use STL format
> - **ASCII**: Not necessary, binary is faster and smaller
> - **Scene Scale**: Enable to ensure correct size
> - **Check Size**: Verify dimensions in slicing software
> - **File Naming**: Use descriptive names with version numbers

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">File Naming</span>
>
> The export tool automatically generates filenames based on:
> - Blender file name (if saved)
> - Object name
> - Format extension
>
> Example: `MyProject-MyModel.stl`
>
> You can change the filename in the file browser when exporting.

---

# Meshy for Godot

# Meshy for Godot

This is the official documentation of Meshy Godot plugin, you'll find detailed instructions on how to use Meshy to create your own 3D models in the Godot editor.

---

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Welcome to the Meshy Godot Plugin Documentation!</span>
>
> In this guide, we will walk you through how to efficiently use this plugin. Learn how to send a model from the official website to a scene with one click.
>
> Let's get started! 🚀

## Overview

<span className="font-bold text-inherit">Meshy Godot Plugin</span> is a Godot plugin that enables seamless import of <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI-generated models.</span> With this plugin, you can effortlessly load and edit 3D assets, significantly enhancing your workflow efficiency.

## Installation

Download the plugin from the <ExternalLink href={"https://www.meshy.ai/integrations/godot"}>Meshy for Godot integration page</ExternalLink>, where you can grab the latest build for your platform.

If there is no addons folder in Godot's FileSystem, create a new one.

   ![godot-plugin-2](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/godot-plugin/2.webp)
   ![godot-plugin-3](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/godot-plugin/3.webp)

Then unzip the downloaded plug-in folder and drag it directly into the addons folder.

   ![godot-plugin-5](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/godot-plugin/5.webp)

Then open the Project Settings, click on the Plugins tab, and enable the Meshy official plugin.

   ![godot-plugin-6](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/godot-plugin/6.webp)

This way, the plugin is installed successfully.

   ![godot-plugin-7](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/godot-plugin/7.webp)

What's more, remember to set the main scene before importing the model.

# Bridge to Omniverse / Isaac Sim
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/omniverse/bridge-to-omniverse

# Bridge to Omniverse / Isaac Sim

Send Meshy 3D models directly into NVIDIA Omniverse or Isaac Sim, with optional Sim-Ready physics and semantic labels applied during import.

---

> **Note:** Before using Send to OV/Isaac, keep Isaac Sim or your Omniverse Kit app running, make sure the Meshy Bridge extension is enabled, and open or create a USD stage.

## Start the Bridge

In the Extensions window, make sure `Meshy Bridge` is enabled. No separate launcher is required.

![Enable Meshy Bridge](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/omniverse-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_ov_enable_bridge.webp)

## Send from Meshy

Open a completed model in your Meshy workspace, click the DCC Bridge menu, and select **Send to OV/Isaac**.

![DCC Bridge menu](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/omniverse-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_sendtodcc.webp)

![Send to OV/Isaac](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/omniverse-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_sendto_ov_isaac.webp)

Meshy sends the model URL, file format, display name, and optional Sim-Ready payload to the local bridge. The extension downloads the asset, converts it to USD when needed, and references it under `/World/<slug>`.

## Configure Sim-Ready

Isaac Sim users can configure the Sim-Ready dialog before sending:

![Sim-Ready dialog](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/omniverse-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_simready_dialog.webp)

- `Semantic Class`: a simple class label such as `chair`, `table`, or `robot`. The bridge writes it through modern semantic labels and also keeps legacy `SemanticsAPI("class")` compatibility.
- `Wikidata QCode`: optional semantic taxonomy label, such as `Q15026`. Empty is allowed; invalid formats are rejected before sending.
- `Height (m)`: optional real-world height override. Empty keeps the source layer and stage unit scaling.
- `Body Type`: `dynamic`, `kinematic`, or `static`.
- `Mass`: defaults to `Auto`. Auto sends no `mass` or `density`; `Mass` sends kilograms; `Density` sends kg/m³.
- `Collision Approximation`: `convexHull`, `convexDecomposition`, `meshSimplification`, `boundingCube`, `boundingSphere`, or `none`. SDF is not supported in this release. Dynamic bodies only allow `convexHull`, `convexDecomposition`, `boundingCube`, and `boundingSphere`.
- `Static Friction`, `Dynamic Friction`, and `Restitution`: physics material values bound to the imported colliders.

## Verify Import

After the request succeeds, the model appears in the active stage under `/World/<slug>`. For Sim-Ready imports, descendant meshes receive `UsdPhysics.CollisionAPI` and `UsdPhysics.MeshCollisionAPI`; dynamic and kinematic wrappers also receive `UsdPhysics.RigidBodyAPI` and `UsdPhysics.MassAPI`.

![Imported result](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/omniverse-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_ov_import_result.webp)

Press Play in Isaac Sim to test physics behavior. Dynamic bodies should simulate, static bodies remain fixed, and kinematic bodies can be driven by animation or script while participating in collision.

## Troubleshooting

- If Meshy cannot connect, confirm Isaac Sim or Kit is running and the extension is enabled.
- If `/status` does not respond, confirm no other process is using port `5331`, then reload the extension.
- If import fails with `no active USD stage`, create or open a stage before sending.
- If a dynamic import rejects `none` or `meshSimplification`, choose a convex or bounding approximation.
- If a QCode is rejected, use the Wikidata format `Q` followed by a non-zero integer, for example `Q15026`.

## Supported Models

Send to OV/Isaac supports all Meshy model types, including animated models.

![Animated model in OV/Isaac](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/omniverse-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_ov_animated_model.webp)

---

# Meshy for Omniverse / Isaac Sim
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/omniverse/introduction

# Meshy for Omniverse / Isaac Sim

Use the Meshy Omniverse Bridge to send Meshy-generated 3D models directly into an active NVIDIA Omniverse or Isaac Sim stage.

---

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Welcome to the Meshy Omniverse / Isaac Sim Bridge Documentation!</span>
>
>   In this guide, we will walk you through how to use this extension. The documentation is divided into two main sections:
>   - Plugin Introduction - Learn about installation and setup requirements.
>   - Bridge to Omniverse - Learn how to send a model from Meshy to an active Omniverse or Isaac Sim stage.
>
>   Let's get started!🚀

## Prerequisite

<span className="font-bold text-inherit">Meshy Omniverse Bridge</span> sends <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI-generated models</span> to the active USD stage in NVIDIA Omniverse or Isaac Sim. It can also apply Sim-Ready body type, collision, physics material, height, semantic class, and optional Wikidata QCode settings during import.

To use Meshy-for-Omniverse / Isaac Sim, you should follow the following steps:

- Download <ExternalLink href={"https://www.meshy.ai/integrations/omniverse"}>Meshy-Omniverse-Bridge</ExternalLink>.

- Register a Meshy account.

ATTENTION: We have tested the following Isaac Sim version: `Isaac Sim 6.0.0`

![Omniverse Bridge overview](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/omniverse-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_ov_download.webp)

## Installation

In Isaac Sim or your Omniverse Kit app, open `Window > Extensions`, click the menu icon (`☰`), choose `Import Extension`, then select the downloaded Meshy Bridge zip package.

![Open Extensions](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/omniverse-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_ov_open_extensions.webp)

![Import Extension menu](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/omniverse-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_ov_import_extension_menu.webp)

![Select Meshy Bridge zip](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/omniverse-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_ov_import_extension_zip.webp)

## Enable the Extension

Search for `Meshy Bridge` in the Extension Manager, enable it, and turn on Autoload if you want it to start automatically next time.

![Enable Meshy Bridge](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/omniverse-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_ov_enable_bridge.webp)

When enabled, the bridge listens on `127.0.0.1:5331` and exposes `/status` and `/import` for the Meshy webapp. If the app is closed or the extension is disabled, Meshy cannot connect to Omniverse.

## Sim-Ready Support

When sending to Omniverse / Isaac Sim, Meshy can apply Sim-Ready settings during import:

- Body type: `dynamic`, `kinematic`, or `static`.
- Mass mode: `Auto`, `Mass`, or `Density`. Auto does not author `mass` or `density`; the physics runtime uses its normal defaults and collider data.
- Collision approximation: `convexHull`, `convexDecomposition`, `meshSimplification`, `boundingCube`, `boundingSphere`, or `none`. SDF collision is not exposed in this release.
- Dynamic bodies only allow convex or bounding approximations. `none` and `meshSimplification` are reserved for static or kinematic bodies.
- Semantic labels: `class` plus an optional `wikidata_qcode`. QCode is optional and must use the Wikidata format, such as `Q15026`.

## Next Steps

After installation, continue to [Bridge to Omniverse](/webapp/plugins/omniverse/bridge-to-omniverse) to send a Meshy model into your stage and verify the Sim-Ready import.

---

# Bridge to Roblox

# Bridge to Roblox

Learn how to use the Meshy Roblox Bridge to send 3D models directly to your Roblox account and use them in Roblox Studio with one click.

---

> **Note:** Before you begin, make sure you have downloaded and installed the Meshy Roblox Bridge. For detailed instructions, please refer to the [Introduction](/webapp/plugins/roblox/introduction) section.

> **Note:** Meshy now supports Roblox bridging directly from the workspace. Pro members and above can send models to Roblox following the steps below.

## Connect Your Roblox Account

In the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI workspace</span>, click the
<span className="font-bold text-inherit">DCC Bridge</span> menu and select
<span className="font-bold text-inherit">Send to Roblox</span>.

   ![Meshy-SendToDCC](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_sendtodcc.webp)

   ![SendToRoblox](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_sendtoroblox.webp)

dialog will appear. Click <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Connect</span>
to open an authorization popup.

   ![Roblox-ConnectDialog](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_connect.webp)

A Roblox authorization page opens in your browser. Log in, review the requested permissions, select the account to grant access, and confirm:

At the same time, the local Bridge app also confirms the account binding:

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_bridge_account.webp"
 alt="Roblox Bridge local app showing account bound" style={{maxWidth: "250px", width: "100%", height: "auto"}} />

## Switch Account
If you need to send models to a different Roblox account after login, you can switch accounts in two ways:

1. **Directly from the Connect dialog** — Click the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Switch Account</span> link at the bottom. This will disconnect the current account and start a new authorization flow.

2. **From the DCC Bridge menu** — Hover over the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Roblox</span> item in the DCC Bridge menu and click the user-switch icon that appears on the right. Then the connect dialog will appear.

## Sending Models to Roblox

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Recommended Workflow</span>
>
> For the best results and to avoid exceeding the Roblox 20 MB upload limit, we recommend completing your model in this order: **Generate → Remesh → Texture**. Remeshing reduces the polygon count and file size, making the model much more likely to upload successfully.

Once your Roblox account is connected, you can send models directly via the DCC Bridge menu without needing to authorize again.

   ![Roblox-Bridge-Connected](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_bridge_connected.webp)

Navigate to the model you want in your
<span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI workspace</span> and click
<span className="font-bold text-inherit">Send to Roblox</span> from the DCC Bridge menu.

Any 3D model you generate in your workspace can be sent to Roblox via the
<span className="font-bold text-inherit">DCC Bridge</span>.

   ![MoreDCC](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_moredcc.webp)

Likewise, models from the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI community</span> are
fully supported and can also be sent to Roblox using the DCC Bridge.

   ![Meshy-Community](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc-community.webp)

## Using Your Model
After the upload completes, the local Bridge app is automatically brought to the foreground. You can access your model through the quick actions on the Bridge app:
{/* TODO: replace with actual screenshot */}
   ![Roblox-Bridge-Complete](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_bridge_complete.webp)

**Copy Asset ID** — Copies the Roblox asset ID to your clipboard for easy reference

**Creator Hub** — Click <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Creator Hub</span> on the model card to open your Roblox Creator Hub inventory and manage the asset
   ![Roblox-CreatorHub](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_creatorhub.webp)

> **Note:** The Creator Hub web preview may not display textures correctly for larger models. This is a limitation of the Roblox web viewer only — your model's textures will appear normally when imported into Roblox Studio.

**Open in Studio** — Click <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Open in Studio</span> on the model card. Roblox Studio will launch and open a default scene containing only the model you just uploaded. This is a temporary preview scene specifically for viewing this asset.

   ![Roblox-Studio-Model](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_studio_model.webp)

**Find it manually** — Open Roblox Studio, go to the
<span className="font-bold text-inherit">Toolbox</span>, select
<span className="font-bold text-inherit">Inventory</span>, then
<span className="font-bold text-inherit">My Packages</span>. All models you have sent via the Bridge will appear here.

   ![Roblox-Toolbox-MyPackages](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_toolbox_packages.webp)

## Upload History
The Bridge app keeps a record of all models you've sent to Roblox. Expand the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Upload History</span> section in the Bridge window to view them.

{/* TODO: replace with actual screenshot */}
   ![Roblox-Bridge-History](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_bridge_history.webp)

For each uploaded model, you can:

- Click **Creator Hub** / **Open in Studio** / **Copy Asset ID** to quickly access the model
- Click the **✕** button to delete an individual record
- Click **Clear All** to remove all upload history

> **Note:** - Upload history is stored locally on your computer. Clearing it does not affect the assets already uploaded to your Roblox account.
> - You can only access models uploaded under the currently logged-in account.

## Troubleshooting

| Issue | Cause | Solution |
| ----- | ----- | -------- |
| "Bridge not running" message in Meshy | The Bridge app is not open | Download and run the Meshy Roblox Bridge app, then try again |
| Authorization popup is blocked | Browser blocked the popup window | Allow popups for the Meshy site in your browser settings |
| "Model exceeds Roblox upload size limit (20MB)" | The GLB file is larger than 20 MB | Use Meshy's remesh feature to reduce the model's polygon count before sending |
| "Upload timed out. Please check your Roblox inventory." | Roblox processing took longer than 3 minutes | Check your Creator Hub inventory — the asset may have uploaded successfully despite the timeout |
| "Lost connection to Roblox Bridge" | Bridge stopped responding during upload | Restart the Bridge app and try again |
| "Upload failed. Please try again." | Roblox API returned an error | Check that the Bridge is still running and your Roblox account is connected, then retry |

# Meshy for Roblox
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/roblox/introduction

# Meshy for Roblox

This is the official documentation of Meshy Roblox Bridge, you'll find detailed instructions on how to send Meshy-generated 3D models to your Roblox account and use them in Roblox Studio.

---

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Welcome to the Meshy Roblox Bridge Documentation!</span>
>
> In this guide, we will walk you through how to efficiently use this bridge. The documentation covers:
>
> - **[Introduction](/webapp/plugins/roblox/introduction)** – Learn about installation and requirements
> - **[Bridge to Roblox](/webapp/plugins/roblox/bridge-to-roblox)** – Learn how to send models from Meshy to Roblox with one click
>
> Let's get started! 🚀

## Prerequisite

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Note for users in Mainland China</span>
>
> Roblox in mainland China is operated by a regional partner with a separate account system and no Open Cloud API support. As a result, Meshy Roblox Bridge **does not work** with Roblox accounts in Mainland China (`roblox.qq.com` / `roblox.cn`).
>
> To use the Bridge, you need:
> 1. A **network proxy / VPN** to access `roblox.com`.
> 2. A **global Roblox account** registered at [roblox.com](https://www.roblox.com)

<span className="font-bold text-inherit">Meshy Roblox Bridge</span> enables seamless upload of
<span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI-generated models</span> to your Roblox account,
where they appear in your Creator Hub inventory and can be used directly in Roblox Studio.

To use it, you need:

- A **Meshy Pro** account or above
- A **Roblox account**
- **macOS** or **Windows** (to run the Bridge app locally)
- The **Meshy Roblox Bridge** app downloaded and running on your computer

## Installation

**Step 1 — Download the Bridge**

Download the [Meshy Roblox Bridge](https://www.meshy.ai/integrations/roblox) app from its integration page.

**Step 2 — Run the Bridge**

Unzip the downloaded file and run the executable:

- **macOS**: Open `Meshy Roblox Bridge`
- **Windows**: Run `MeshyRobloxBridge.exe`

The Bridge starts a local server on port `5330`. Keep it running in the background while you use Meshy.

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Bridge Status</span>
>
> The Bridge must be running before you can send models to Roblox. If you see a "Bridge not running" message in Meshy, make sure the app is open on your computer. Also ensure port `5330` is not blocked by your firewall.

## macOS Gatekeeper
Since the Meshy Roblox Bridge is distributed outside the Mac App Store and may not be notarized by Apple, macOS Gatekeeper can block it from opening. If you see a warning like **"MeshyRobloxBridge can't be opened because Apple cannot check it for malicious software"**, follow the steps below to allow it.

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_gatekeeper_warning.webp"
 alt="macOS Gatekeeper warning dialog" style={{maxWidth: "420px", width: "100%", height: "auto"}} />

**Option A — Allow via System Settings (recommended)**

1. After the warning dialog appears, click <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Done</span> to dismiss it.
2. Open <span className="font-bold text-inherit">System Settings → Privacy & Security</span>.
3. Scroll down to the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Security</span> section. You will see a message saying **"MeshyRobloxBridge" was blocked from use because it is not from an identified developer**.

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_gatekeeper_settings.webp"
 alt="macOS Privacy and Security settings showing blocked app" style={{maxWidth: "580px", width: "100%", height: "auto"}} />

4. Click <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Open Anyway</span>. A dialog will pop up asking you to select <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Open Anyway</span> again to confirm.

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_gatekeeper_open.webp"
 alt="macOS Open Anyway confirmation dialog" style={{maxWidth: "420px", width: "100%", height: "auto"}} />

5. macOS will then ask you to enter your Mac login password to authorize the action.

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_gatekeeper_password.webp"
 alt="macOS password prompt to allow the app" style={{maxWidth: "360px", width: "100%", height: "auto"}} />

After entering your password, the Bridge will launch successfully. You should see the Bridge window showing <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Server: Running</span>.

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/roblox-plugin/v0.1.0/doc_roblox_bridge_running.webp"
 alt="Meshy Roblox Bridge running" style={{maxWidth: "250px", width: "100%", height: "auto"}} />

**Option B — Allow via Terminal**

If you prefer using the command line, open <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Terminal</span> and run:

```bash
xattr -cr /path/to/MeshyRobloxBridge.app
```

Replace `/path/to/MeshyRobloxBridge.app` with the actual path to the app — for example, `~/Downloads/MeshyRobloxBridge.app`. After running the command, double-click the app to open it normally.

> **Note:** This is a one-time step. Once you allow the app, macOS will remember your choice and you won't see the Gatekeeper warning again.

---

# Bridge to Unity

Learn how to use the DCC Bridge to seamlessly import Meshy 3D models directly into your Unity scenes.

---

> **Note:** Meshy now supports Unity bridging directly from the workspace. Pro members and above can send models to Unity following the steps below.

## Run Bridge in Meshy-Unity Plugin

Click bridge on the Meshy drop-down menu to open the Meshy Bridge window. Click <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Run Bridge</span> to initialize and start the bridge connection.

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/unity-plugin/v0.2.2/doc_unity_panel.webp" alt="Unity-plugin-19" width="300px" style={{width: "500px", height: "auto"}} />

## Sending Models to Unity

Navigate to the model you want in your <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI workspace</span>, click the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">DCC Bridge</span> menu, and select <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Send to Unity</span>.

   ![Meshy-SentToDCC](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/unity-plugin/v0.2.2/doc_sendtodcc.webp)

   ![SendToUnity](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/unity-plugin/v0.2.2/doc_sendtounity.webp)

   ![Unity-plugin-result](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/unity-plugin/v0.2.2/doc_unity_result.webp)

Any 3D model you generate in your workspace can be effortlessly imported into <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Unity</span> via the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">DCC Bridge</span>.

   ![MoreDCC](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/unity-plugin/v0.2.2/doc-moredcc.webp)

Likewise, models published by other users in the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI community</span> are fully supported and can also be seamlessly imported into Unity using the DCC Bridge integration.

# Meshy for Unreal
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/unreal/introduction

# Meshy for Unreal

This is the official documentation of Meshy Unreal plugin, you'll find detailed instructions on how to use Meshy to create your own 3D models in the Unreal editor.

---

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Welcome to the Meshy Unreal Plugin Documentation!</span>
>
> In this guide, we will walk you through how to efficiently use this plugin. Learn how to send a model from the official website to a scene with one click.
>
> Let's get started! 🚀

## Overview

<span className="font-bold text-inherit">Meshy Unreal Plugin</span> is a Unreal plugin that enables seamless import of <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI-generated models.</span> With this plugin, you can effortlessly load and edit 3D assets, significantly enhancing your workflow efficiency.

## Installation

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Engine version compatibility:</span> The plugin ships a separate build for each Unreal Engine version. Download the build that matches your engine (UE 5.4–5.7, plus a source package) from the <ExternalLink href={"https://www.meshy.ai/integrations/unreal-engine"}>Meshy for Unreal Engine integration page</ExternalLink>.

There are two ways to use the plugin:
1. Install to the Engine Directory:
  - Windows:
The plugin can be placed directly in the C:\Program Files\Epic Games\Unreal_5.0\Engine\Plugins directory.
  - Mac:
The plugin can be placed directly in the /Users/Shared/Epic Games/Unreal_5.5/Engine/Plugins directory.
2. Install to the Project Directory:
The plugin can also be placed in the Plugins directory of the project. If this directory does not exist, you can create it.

In this way, the plugin will be installed successfully.

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/unreal-plugin/2.png" alt="unteal-plugin-2" width="300px" style={{width: "500px", height: "auto"}} />

# Troubleshooting
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/unreal/troubleshooting

# Troubleshooting

Learn how to troubleshoot common issues when using the Meshy Unreal Plugin.

---

## Textures appear blurry

After the model is imported into Unreal, if the texture appears blurry, and only by clicking the corresponding asset of the model in the Content Browser will the texture become clear again. The solution to this problem is to enter `r.Streaming.FullyLoadUsedTextures 1` in the box at the bottom right corner of the Unreal editor, as shown in the figure. After entering this command, the texture will become clear again.

![unreal-plugin-14](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/unreal-plugin/14.png)

# Bridge to ZBrush
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/zbrush/bridge-to-zbrush

# Bridge to ZBrush

Learn how to quickly send assets from the Meshy web application directly to ZBrush using our bridge feature.

---

> **Note:** Meshy supports ZBrush bridging directly from the workspace. Pro members and above can send models to ZBrush following the steps below. Requires **ZBrush 2025.1+** with the Meshy plugin installed — see [Introduction](/webapp/plugins/zbrush/introduction).

## Run the Bridge

In ZBrush, open **ZPlugin → Meshy Bridge** and click **Load Meshy Bridge**.

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/load-meshy-bridge.webp" alt="zbrush-plugin-load-meshy-bridge" style={{width: "360px", height: "auto"}} />

In the **Meshy** palette, confirm that **Run Bridge** is highlighted **orange** — that means the bridge is enabled and listening for models sent from Meshy.

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/run-bridge-orange.webp" alt="zbrush-plugin-run-bridge-orange" style={{width: "500px", height: "auto"}} />

## Sending Models to ZBrush

Navigate to the model you want in your <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI workspace</span>, click the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">DCC Bridge</span> menu, and select <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Send to ZBrush</span>.

   ![Meshy-SendToDCC](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/send-to-dcc.webp)

   ![SendToZBrush](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/send-to-zbrush.webp)

The model is downloaded in the background and queued for import.

## Importing Pending Models

Because of a ZBrush plugin limitation, the model is not imported the moment it arrives — you import it manually. In the **Meshy** palette, click **Import Pending**.

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/import-pending.webp" alt="zbrush-plugin-import-pending" style={{width: "500px", height: "auto"}} />

The model goes straight into the **Tool** panel as a white model with **BasicMaterial** applied by default.

   ![zbrush-plugin-imported-tool](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/imported-tool.webp)

For models that carry a **Base Color** texture, go to **Tool → Texture Map** and pick the map whose name matches your model to turn it on. The bridge has already imported the corresponding texture file and applied **Flip V** for you, so no extra setup is needed.

   ![zbrush-plugin-texture-map](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/texture-map.webp)

If you'd rather the bridge import for you, click **Wait for Model**. For the next 90 seconds ZBrush waits for a model-send task from Meshy and imports it automatically as soon as it arrives.

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/wait-for-model.webp" alt="zbrush-plugin-wait-for-model" style={{width: "500px", height: "auto"}} />

> **Note:** While **Wait for Model** is active, ZBrush is blocked from other operations until a model arrives or the 90-second window ends.

## More Ways to Send

Any 3D model you generate in your workspace — regardless of how it was created — can be sent to ZBrush via the DCC Bridge, from the workspace toolbar or a model's overview page.

   ![zbrush-plugin-more-entries](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/more-entries.webp)

Likewise, models published by other users in the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI community</span> are fully supported and can also be seamlessly sent to ZBrush.

   ![zbrush-plugin-community](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/community.webp)

---

# Meshy for ZBrush
Source: https://docs.meshy.ai/webapp/plugins/zbrush/introduction

# Meshy for ZBrush

This is the official documentation of the Meshy ZBrush plugin. You'll find detailed instructions on how to install the plugin and import the models you generated in Meshy directly onto the ZBrush canvas for sculpting.

---

> **Note:** <span className="font-bold text-inherit">Welcome to the Meshy ZBrush Plugin Documentation!</span>
>
> In this guide, we will walk you through how to efficiently use this plugin. The documentation covers:
>
> - **[Plugin Introduction](/webapp/plugins/zbrush/introduction)** – Learn about prerequisites and installation
> - **[Bridge to ZBrush](/webapp/plugins/zbrush/bridge-to-zbrush)** – Learn how to quickly send assets to ZBrush from the webapp
>
> Let's get started! 🚀

## Overview

<span className="font-bold text-inherit">Meshy ZBrush Plugin</span> is a plugin that brings <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI-generated models</span> into a running ZBrush session. ZBrush is a sculpting tool, so the bridge imports clean **OBJ** geometry straight onto the canvas as a starting point for your sculpt (base color is applied where available). Imported models are saved as ZTools under `ZTools/Meshy`.

Because ZBrush's embedded Python cannot host a server, the plugin runs a small background bridge process that listens for models sent from Meshy and hands them to the **Meshy** palette inside ZBrush.

## Prerequisite

- **ZBrush 2025.1 or later** — the plugin relies on the official ZBrush Python API. Older versions are not supported.
- **macOS or Windows** — download the build for your platform (a macOS `.dmg` or a Windows `.zip`). Each installer bundles its own Python runtime, so no separate Python install is needed.
- **A Meshy Pro account or above** — required to use the DCC Bridge.

## Installation

In your <span className="font-bold text-inherit">MeshyAI workspace</span>, open the <span className="font-bold text-inherit">DCC Bridge</span> and click the **download** button next to ZBrush.

   ![zbrush-plugin-dcc-bridge-download](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/dcc-bridge-download.webp)

This opens the ZBrush plugin detail page. Choose your platform and download the matching build — the **macOS `.dmg`** or the **Windows `.zip`**.

   ![zbrush-plugin-detail-download](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/plugin-detail-download.webp)

Open the downloaded build (on macOS, open the `.dmg`; on Windows, extract the `.zip`) and copy **`MeshyBridge.zsc`** and the **`MeshyBridgeData`** folder into ZBrush's plugin directory, `ZData/ZPlugs64`:

- **macOS** — e.g. `/Applications/Maxon ZBrush 2026/ZData/ZPlugs64`
- **Windows** — e.g. `C:\Program Files\Maxon ZBrush 2026\ZData\ZPlugs64`

   ![zbrush-plugin-zplugs64](https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/zplugs64.webp)

> **Note:** **macOS only:** the build is not notarized, so macOS quarantines the bundled runtime on first download. If you skip this step, ZBrush fails to launch the bundled Python and shows an error like the one below.
>
>    <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/macos-error.webp" alt="zbrush-plugin-macos-error" style={{width: "360px", height: "auto"}} />
>
> After copying the files into `ZPlugs64`, clear the quarantine flag once so ZBrush can launch the bundled Python:
>
> ```bash
> xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Maxon ZBrush 2026/ZData/ZPlugs64/MeshyBridgeData"
> ```

Restart ZBrush, then open **ZPlugin → Meshy Bridge → Load Meshy Bridge**. After a few seconds, a new **Meshy** menu appears in ZBrush's **top menu bar** (the same row as Zplugin, Render, Tool, etc.) — that **Meshy** menu is where all the bridge controls live. The plugin is installed successfully.

   <img src="https://cdn.meshy.ai/docs-assets/zbrush-plugin/v0.1.0/zplugin-menu.webp" alt="zbrush-plugin-zplugin-menu" style={{width: "360px", height: "auto"}} />

---

🚀 Next, head to **[Bridge to ZBrush](/webapp/plugins/zbrush/bridge-to-zbrush)** to send your first model from the Meshy webapp.

---
